column5: TCL - 115" QM7K Series 4K UHD QD Mini LED Smart TV with Google TV (2025)
column8: review1 - This TV is absolutely fantastic once you take the time to tweak the picture settings. The picture quality is out of this world—vivid, sharp, and immersive. Black levels are surprisingly deep and comparable to OLED, which is impressive for a display this size. I don’t use the built-in TCL Google TV interface, since I prefer running everything through my Apple TV, and it works flawlessly that way. That said, you really need 4K content at this size. Anything below 4K—especially 1080p or worse—doesn’t scale well and is very noticeable. Once you’re feeding it 4K, though, it’s breathtaking. The only real challenge I’ve run into is finding the right TV stand. This TV is massive and heavy, so it needs a very sturdy, wide stand. I eventually found one, but at 18” high it places the screen a bit too high for comfortable viewing—I end up straining my neck. Ideally, I’d love to find a stand closer to 12” high that can handle the weight, but options are extremely limited. Overall, if you can solve the stand/mounting situation and have plenty of 4K content, this TV is hands-down one of the best viewing experiences you can get today. ||| review2 - I splurged for black friday and got it for a good price. column5: Samsung - 55" Class U7900 Series UHD 4K Smart Tizen TV (2025)
column8: review1 - I’m extremely happy with my 55-inch Samsung TV. The picture quality is outstanding—colors are vibrant, the contrast is sharp, and everything looks incredibly clear whether I’m watching movies, sports, or streaming shows. The 4K resolution really makes a difference, especially with newer content. The sound quality is also surprisingly good for a flat-screen TV, but it pairs perfectly with a soundbar if you want an even more immersive experience. Setup was quick and easy, and the smart features are very user-friendly. I love how fast the apps load and how seamless it is to switch between streaming services. The design is sleek and modern, with a thin bezel that looks great in my living room. Overall, it feels like a high-quality product that delivers excellent performance for the price. I would definitely recommend this TV to anyone looking for a reliable and great-looking upgrade. ||| review2 - I picked this up to replace a 50-inch Samsung that’s about nine years old, and it’s clear the brand hasn’t lost its touch. The picture quality is excellent, with rich colors and a noticeably improved interface compared to older models. The panel isn’t the brightest on the market, but it still performs well in daylight, even with some glare. The redesigned remote is simpler and more intuitive, which pairs well with the TV overall. My only real complaint is that the interface can feel sluggish. It’s not a deal-breaker, but it’s something I don’t typically notice on other TVs in this price range. Overall, it’s a strong upgrade with a few quirks, but nothing that overshadows the solid performance. It would easily earn five stars if the interface weren’t packed with ads and sponsored content. Pairing it with a streaming device or a console and setting the TV to power on to the last used input bypasses most of the UI issues, leaving you with a well-priced panel that performs reliably. ||| review3 - I am extremely impressed with the Samsung 55" U7900 Series! The picture quality is outstanding—crisp 4K detail, vibrant colors, and excellent brightness make movies and sports look incredible. The upscaling is surprisingly good too, so even older content looks sharp. The Tizen interface is fast, intuitive, and packed with apps. Switching between streaming services is seamless, and the remote is simple and responsive. Sound quality is better than I expected for a slim TV, and pairing it with my soundbar via HDMI-ARC was effortless. The design is modern and sleek, and it fits perfectly in my living room. Setup was quick, and the TV automatically recognized my connected devices. Overall, this is an amazing value for a 2025 model—great performance, great features, and great picture quality. Highly recommended! ||| review4 - This was an impulse purchase, that I really didn't need, but I am so happy with it. The size is perfect for me and my space. The picture is amazing. The sound is amazing. It links to my Samsung phone, which I'm still trying to play with, but overall, it was a great purchase. ||| review5 - I was a bit disappointed the first few days we had this tv but I found some bass line settings and mad the adjustments and it’s looking pretty good now. We have a Samsung Q80 in the living room and by comparison there’s no comparison but for the money I’m very happy with this as a bedroom tv. It obviously doesn’t get as bright as the set but it’s bright enough for me.Like a lot of other reviews the remote leaves a lot to be desired especially with older hands it’s very small. ||| review6 - I recently got the Samsung 55" Class U7900 Series UHD 4K Smart Tizen TV (2025), and I absolutely love it! It has completely transformed my viewing experience, and I couldn't be happier. I recently got this TV, and it fits perfectly in my apartment without overpowering the space. Setup was a breeze, and the picture quality is absolutely stunning—crisp, clear, and bursting with vibrant, natural colors. It really elevates my entire viewing experience with its rich sound quality that’s just as impressive. Navigating through its innovative features is surprisingly easy, making watching TV more fun than ever. I love how quickly I can switch between channels and apps, save shows to my library, or return to live TV—everything happens almost instantly. Rewinding live TV to catch a missed line in a show and then seamlessly catching up to the livestream? Absolutely fantastic. I’ve only scratched the surface of what this TV can do, but I already appreciate how streamlined the remote is—super thin and easy to handle. I had to use the manual to figure out the volume control. ||| review8 - The picture definition is incredible, super easy to set up and use. Looks great in a smaller space, even at 55". Sound is excellent. If you have a Samsung phone, using Smart Things to control the TV from anywhere is a nice feature. ||| review9 - I am still getting the hang of my new Samsung 55" TV. Its Smart Tizen operating system is different from that of my other Samsung TV. My enjoyment of that TV gave rise to the current purchase, where undeniably there is a learning arc yet to be traveled. That said, this TV seems to actively thwart channel surfing. The interface is cluttered and difficult to navigate. It forever leaves me without a full picture of what is available to be watched, particularly disappointing where Samsung TV Plus is concerned. Program loading runs the gamut from pokey to minutes-long. I am adapting by learning what is on prior to power up and, once at a channel, am inclined to stay, even to the point of suffering through commercials. (Thank God there is still a mute feature.) AT&T delivers to me ultra fast fiber optic internet speed, so I discount connection issues as an important cause of any slowness. That said, I think my Samsung 55" Class U7900 Series UHD 4K TV is worth the $302 I paid Best Buy to have it appear at my doorstep. Like I said for the price you cant really beat it even with quirks! ||| review8 - I recently upgraded to the Insignia 55″ Class F50 Series LED 4K UHD Smart Fire TV and overall I’m quite pleased. Right out of the box the 4K image looked noticeably sharper and the colors more vibrant compared to my previous 1080p set. The Fire TV interface is intuitive, the Alexa voice remote is handy, and setup was quick. Watching Netflix, YouTube and streaming sports has been really enjoyable — the screen size and clarity make a difference. On the flip side, when watching late at night in a darker room I did notice that the blacks aren’t as deep as those on premium sets I’ve seen, and fast-motion content (especially high-end gaming) lacks the ultra-smoothness of higher refresh-rate TVs. For the price, it delivers a lot more than I expected. The picture quality is surprisingly solid. The 4K resolution is sharp, and colors look vibrant, especially when watching movies or streaming shows in HD or 4K. HDR support helps bring out better contrast between bright and dark scenes, which makes a noticeable difference compared to older TVs. Setup was super easy right out of the box. The built-in Fire TV system made it simple to log into apps like Netflix, YouTube, and Prime Video without needing any extra devices. The Alexa voice remote is a nice touch and makes searching for content quick and convenient. Sound quality is decent but not amazing. It gets the job done for everyday viewing, but if you want a more immersive experience, you’ll probably want to add a soundbar. Where this TV really stands out is the value. Insignia TVs are known for being budget-friendly while still offering solid 4K performance, and this one definitely fits that description. A couple of minor downsides: the interface can feel a little slow at times, and the overall build quality isn’t as premium as higher-end brands. But honestly, for the price point, those are easy trade-offs. My only (sort of) issue is that the local Best Buy store associates can no longer negotiate the price of Clearance Items. column5: LG - 77" Class B5 Series OLED AI 4K UHD Smart webOS TV (2025)
column8: review1 - This TV is absolutely gorgeous. Coming from a plasma with great inky blacks I did not want to upgrade at all but I am glad to have gone OLED. And don't let the "entry level" tag placed on this tv fool you, it's OLED through and through. Beautiful colors and deep pure blacks. And with the right settings, the picture is natural and sharp. I am beyond happy. The speakers are way better than I would have ever thought. My only negative is that OS is sluggish. Overall I highly recommend this TV for exceptional movie watching and gaming. ||| review2 - This LG OLED B5 AI 77” is absolutely worth it. The picture quality is stunning — deep blacks, vibrant colors, and excellent brightness for both movies and sports. Dolby Vision and HDR really make a huge difference. Sound is surprisingly good for a slim TV, but pairing it with a soundbar takes the experience to another level. The design is sleek and modern, and it looks beautiful mounted on the wall. WebOS is very fast and user-friendly, with all the apps I use (Netflix, Prime, Apple TV+, YouTube) running smoothly. Overall, an excellent purchase — premium quality at a great price. column5: TCL - 65" Class QM9K Series 4K UHD HDR QD-Mini LED Smart TV with Google TV (2025)
column8: review1 - I recently bought the TCL QM9K as a gift for my husband. This TV is incredible—the brightness is outstanding, it looks very elegant, and the design is excellent. The sound quality is also impressive. This is the third TCL TV we’ve owned at home, and the first high-end model. The HDR performance is spectacular; I don’t think anything could surpass it. Motion handling on YouTube is very good, and Netflix works well too, although occasionally you can notice some minor distractions or glitches in fast-moving scenes. The serious problem is with Disney Plus: it’s practically impossible to watch content there. The image flickers, lags, and the motion is erratic, and no adjustment seems to fix it. This is frustrating because I also own a 2024 55-inch TCL Mini LED model, and I’ve had no complaints with that one. I didn’t expect to encounter this issue on a high-end model. If I had purchased the QM8K instead, I wouldn’t be facing this problem. I truly hope TCL or Disney Plus can resolve this in the future. I don't suggest you don't buy it until they fix that problem and improve the movement process; you can buy the QMK6 L, K7, or QMK8, which doesn't have these problems. ||| review2 - TCL tv is great . Beautiful picture and sound . Geek Squad was fantastic. ||| review3 - Let’s get to the point. If you're looking for a high-end top of the line TV that pushes the envelope on clarity, brightness, sound quality and smart features, you should consider the TCL QM9K 65 inch. My previous TV was the Vizio M Series 50 inch that I’ve had since 2019. It was and still is a great TV but I thought it was time for an upgrade to see what has changed over the last several years with TV’s, so enter the QM9k. Inside the box came the TV( well protected), the usual paperwork, the stand with necessary screws, cable management clips, the remote( with 2 AAA batteries). Attaching the stand, swapping HDMI cables and placing the TV didn’t take long( ~20 mins) especially if you have two people working on it. You can also mount it if needed but you’ll need the required tools, and likely expertise to get it done properly for your setup. Once powered on you’ll have to go through a few rounds of initial setup options and updates, (it is a smart tv after all), especially if you’re a Google account holder and want to attach your account. This took me around 20~30 mins. I won’t do a spec dumb since that’s easily found on the BestBuy’s page for the QM9K but I will share what I liked. The first thing that struck me was how bright it was. According to TCL it can achieve 6500 nits. This was actually pretty great for me given that my living room gets flushed with a tonne of natural light during the day and based on where I’ve placed the tv the glare would lead me to pull the curtains. But those days are gone, my curtains can now be pulled all day without sunlight affecting my viewing experience. The next thing I noticed was that the screen is near bezel less and it had great viewing angles. When it comes to viewing content, this TV is top notch, especially if you are viewing a lot of HDR content. “Colors pop” would be an understatement , they explode whether you are watching films, sports or gaming. On the topic of gaming this excels! This was set up with my PS5 and no matter what I threw at it, a shooter like The Finals, sports like Fifa or more story driven like Ghost of Yotei (currently playing & loving this) it crushed it. I don’t even know what lag is anymore. Not to forget audio, but the sound from the Bang and Olufsen speakers was definitely an improvement from my previous tv. It is very good but you won’t be getting theater-sounding performance without pairing it with a dedicated sound system, which you can attach either via the HDMI eARC port or through blutooth. So as I’m sure you could have guessed the QM9K is a smart TV but it is just a lil tad bit smarter, as it has Google’s Gemini built. So you can either from the TV’s remote ( ohhh yeah the remote is well designed, intuitive and illuminated!!!) or speaking directly to the TV( it has microphones you can turn off) you can access it just like you would from your phone or computer. The bottom line is you can’t go wrong with the QM9K, you’re getting outstanding performance in many areas and you’ll never wanna look away. ||| review4 - Regarding setup and unboxing the 65 inch TCL QM9K, I am a fairly big guy (6'2") and I was able to set it up by myself although the instructions don't recommend that. The base has two levels you can set it at, one of which is higher in case you have a soundbar which we do. The base/stand provides a convenient area to place our soundbar on. However, it cannot be set back flush with the TV, if it is it will block the sensor on the lower front of the TV so I had to place the soundbar several inches in front of it. Once powered on, the TV will guide you through setting it up which includes logging into your Google account (this is our first Google TV) and that actually goes pretty smoothly in conjunction with your phone. Added bonus, I now have Google Home on my TV so I can change my thermostat or view our security cameras from my television, pretty cool. Our living room has a "cut out" in the wall as was the style of some home builders back in the late 90’s/early 2000's, the intent of which was to recess your TV back into the cutout so its flush with the fireplace. Well, that doesn't really work these days with larger TV screens so ours sits in front of the cutout (see picture). This affects the rear-facing speakers and kind of mutes them. While the Bang and Olufsen speakers are the best sounding built-in TV speakers I've ever heard along with impressive deep bass for such a thin TV, they don't work as good as our front-facing soundbar and subwoofer. According to TCL the screen "features an anti-reflective screen treatment that reduces mirror-like reflections from windows and overhead lights" and this matters in our living room. We have 8 big picture windows which allow tons of light through our living room and its been a problem with previous TVs. But the TCL QM9K has eliminated that, we get no reflections or glaring from our windows anymore. So here's how our TV setup works: we pay for DirecTV service at our cabin up in the Rocky Mountains and we use DirecTV Stream down at our main home since its included with the service. Our previous smart TV did not allow the DirecTV Stream app to be loaded so we had to use a streaming device, in our case a Roku Ultra. When I first setup the TCL QM9K I also connected the Roku Ultra just by default assuming I'd need it. Turns out the DirecTV Stream app is compatible with Google TV so that is convenient. But more importantly, I compared the picture using both methods and the difference is significant. When I first tested this viewing through the Roku Ultra the picture is great, but when viewing directly through the TCL it becomes phenomenal. It is stunningly crystal clear with bright gorgeous colors and deep blacks. When I'd switch back through the Roku Ultra the picture looks duller, more pixelated and the colors are muted. Switching back to viewing through the TCL the picture just comes alive. It is so good it looks almost like 3D, I was amazed at the difference. I also compared the pictures for viewing through the TCL vs Roku for other streaming apps like Netflix and found the differences to be less dramatic with the nod being given to the TCL as it always seemed brighter and clearer but the differences weren't huge, not like the case for the DirecTV Stream app. So to sum this up, the TCL has eliminated the need for our Roku and the picture is simply incredible. Regarding the Ambient Display, I like the idea. Per TCL's description: "With the Ambient Mode Sensor, the TCL QM9K detects your presence and responds. Enter the room and the screen lights up with a clean screensaver or helpful widgets you choose. Step away and it shuts off to save energy and reduce distractions." I have checked and doublechecked all the settings, read and re-read the user guide, searched the internet, watch videos, etc., to ensure its active and setup correctly but I just can't make it work. It has never turned on or off as described and I'm positive my soundbar isn't blocking the ambient sensor but it just does not work as expected. Then this morning as my wife was watching the TV it just shut off without warning. So I’m thinking its user error and I’ve setup something incorrectly in the ambient display settings but it doesn’t matter since my wife asked me to turn off that function and we’ll just stick with old school and use the remote power button. Speaking of the remote, its backlit which I love and works great. For example, using our old Roku remote you’d have to point it directly at the soundbar to adjust the volume as it uses infrared (IR). With the TCL remote that’s not necessary as it uses radio frequency (RF) to adjust volume and that works way better. I also love the screensaver which I configured to my Google Photos. I could sit there and watch it for hours viewing photos I haven't seen in years. However, the screensaver has never actually gone into 'screensaver mode' when I’ve had the TV on. I have had to turn it on manually with a quick click of the power button. I’ve tested it numerous times by leaving the TV idle but it has never come on based on my Screensaver settings. Then last night while my wife was watching a movie and said she got a message from the TV a couple of times saying the screensaver was about to turn on. She had to override that message a few times which was kind of annoying during the movie so I think this is related to my inability to make the ambient display work properly. Pretty sure its user error as I’m still trying to figure that out and why it doesn't seem to work as described. I am certainly not knocking off any stars in my review for that as this is one awesome television with the best picture I have ever seen, a rich feature set that's easy to use and dial it in as I like, and excellent sound (even though I prefer my soundbar). Five stars, no doubt about it. ||| review5 - My previous TVs have all been budget brand. They were great, but they are not even in the same universe as the TCL QM9K. My oldest daughter recently moved out, so my wife and I decided to turn her old room into the movie/game (PS5) room. Being the central area for movies and gaming, we wanted a better TV. The QM9K absolutely delivered. I don't know if there is a better TV out there at the moment. First, it's packaged nicely. I installed it by myself, which was a little tricky. I recommend two people to put the stand on and put it where you want it. To install the stand, I used two of the side protector Styrofoam pieces to lift the bottom corners to install the stand. I will say that the specs list the stand as 47" wide, it's not. It actually measures 15.25" wide by 14.5" deep. It easily fits on a small dresser (our temporary spot until I mount it). It is a compact stand that doesn't take up much space, but it is deep enough to be very stable. Initial setup is easy. If you have the Google Home app, you can add it and it can import settings from the app. It also has Gemini built in. If you have the microphone on, you can say, "Hey Google, turn on/off the TV", plus anything else you want Gemini to do. There is a separate light at the bottom of the center panel where the power light is that comes on when it is listening. You can also set it to ambient mode when you walk in the room. The first thing I did after setup was watch a movie. It was night time and this TV is insanely bright. I also watched during the day and with two windows across from the TV and the sun hitting them, it was still bright and easy to see. I then watched a YouTube video that was 4K HDR of various scenes with a lot of color and contrast. (The pictures are from that video). With this TV having 6,000 local dimming zones, blacks are pure black and colors explode. I've never seen a TV this good with colors, blacks, contrast and saturation. It is absolutely top-tier. I have always had a soundbar for my living room TV, but with these speakers, I don't think I will be getting a soundbar. The sound is loud, clear and deep. It's the only TV that I've seen where you can see speakers on the back. It is plenty of sound for the smaller bedroom that we have it in. The remote is backlit, which I believe should just be the standard now. I will say that for me, the remote is a little lacking. It does have voice control and dedicated buttons for Netflix, Prime Video, Free TV, and YouTube. However, it doesn't have dedicated buttons for rewind, play/pause and fast forward. I would like to still have those buttons. I watch a lot of YouTube videos and to pause it, I have to hit the center button which brings up the progress bar on the video and then press it again to actually pause it. It would be nice if it was just one button press. Fast forward and rewind are the left and right side of the circle. Not terrible, and it's just me being nit-picky. For comparison, my budget TV remote has buttons for Netflix, YouTube, Prime Video, Disney+, Tubi, and a "favorite" button that is customizable to the app of your choice. I have that set to Hulu. It does have a play/pause button, but rewind and fast forward are the left and right of the circle button. Just having that play/pause button is great. I wish the QM9K remote had it. Again, nothing huge, just something I wish it had. Overall, this TV is in a class by itself. If you're looking for a TV, I cannot recommend the QM9K enough. It has absolutely blown me away. ||| review6 - Ok, so I’m upgrading from a standard 4k to this beast. Even though my previous tv was 4k, it doesn’t even compare to some of the features. Setup. It’s pretty standard. I thought it was a tad confusing, but realized I was over analyzing it. It’s super easy to setup. Honestly taking it out of the box took longer than hooking up the base and setting it upright. I like how you can wall mount it or use the base. The base has two levels. One is lower or the other is higher if you have a soundbar. Powering on and running the update took about 15 mins, but that’s probably my internet connection at the time. I’m still messing around with the perfect settings, but I’m super happy so far. The refresh rate, the picture quality and sound are amazing. I love the built in subwoofer. It’s making my hockey watching so fun! Visually all the colors are popping magnificently. Sports are crisp and vibrant. The reds and black tones don’t disappoint. I was blown away at the red from the 49ers football jerseys. It was so impressive how rich the red color was. The refresh is quick and something I’m still getting use to it since I didn’t really use it with my previous tv. I was impressed with how the transition from Hulu to Disney+ to Netflix went. I still have to work on the refresh and color levels. But I was impressed with the basics. The room the tv is in is really bright, so I can make the adjustments for that. The sound has been impressive. I don’t think you need a subwoofer. It was great watching sports and then streaming something for the kids. Pros: 4K Apps Mobile app Dolby vision Motion rate 480 144Hz refresh rate 4 HDMIs HDR10 Smart capable Google voice Comfy and style remote Cons: Nothing so far Overall: This is simply amazing. I’ve loved every minute. I’m debating on streaming or using something like a Roku device and use a high quality hdmi to see the difference. I know it’s expensive, but you can’t go wrong with this beast. Now I want to get a ps5! ||| review7 - Setup: With it being a Google TV, signing in and updating the TV didn't take long, only a few minutes. The usual apps like YouTube, Netflix, etc. all are accessible directly from the TV. There was no lag selecting or using the apps like I've had on other lower end smart TVs. Adding channels from my antenna was also relatively quick. The tuner seemed to be pretty good as it picked up a lot of local channels. Picture: The contrast is amazing. The blacks actually look black while other colors look bright. I watched a few of my 4K movies and they were very clear. Does a great job. ||| review16 - [Employee of bestbuy] So far the tv is excellent with great picture and sound! ||| review17 - TCL has been an emerging TV powerhouse in the US market since 2013 and is now the fastest growing TV brand in America. I admit I haven’t been as familiar with TCL because in the beginning they focused more on budget-oriented Roku style tv’s. But choosing to focus on that product allowed them to grow and expand their lineup to more higher end premium tv’s. I have been loyal to Samsung the last 15 years but with the QM9K QLED Mini LED TV, their latest flagship model, TCL now has my attention. This TV is by far one of the best I’ve ever tested and should seriously be on your short list of considerations if you’re in the market. Initial unboxing of the tv was easy and straight forward. We had the stand on in less than a few minutes and were rocking and ready to go. First impressions of the tv itself is it feels very high end. The minimal frame on the outside of the tv compared to our old family room Samsung is a nice change. The tv isn’t overly heavy for a 65 inch and will be easy to mount over the fireplace once I get some help installing this weekend. The cable management straps are a nice touch to help keep everything neat and orderly. The remote that comes with the QM9K is fully integrated with Google Voice and is easily paired to the tv. Just wish they had put the Power Button on the top left corner, I’ve inadvertently muted my TV a few times now because they put the power button on the right side, but I’ll adjust! Setup with Google TV is as seamless a process as you’ll find. I love the Google UI and the ability to pre-load your favorite apps. Coming from a 7-year-old Samsung in our main living room area it’s strikingly apparent how old, outdated and basic the software was. Google TV feels like a whole new TV experience, especially with the introduction of AI and Gemini. Gemini is just scratching the surface of capabilities. Some of the highlights are you can use it to answer debates among family members with detailed answers to questions. Point towards helpful YouTube videos to solve how to problems at home. It can recommend new shows based on preferences or even do season recaps of shows to help you catch up. It can even help you find a TV show by vaguely describing it like how Apple Music works with lyrics. Hands free access with “Hey Google” is possible as well as well as automation of Google Home devices connected to your home network. My favorite feature so far is the ability to have it detect when someone enters the room and turn on to standby mode which will either display art or photos loaded to your Google Account. There are also additional widgets that can display weather, news, as well. The Technical Specs on this tv are impressive. If you’re considering this model you probably have done some homework already on features, so I won’t dive too deep into the technical aspects of this tv. Just know the Q9K is an absolute monster with every feature you could possibly need. The colors and brightness on this tv are phenomenal. Rich beautiful depth of color with amazing contrast. The Mini-LED and 6500 Nits of brightness provide such a clear, bright and consistent picture. The anti-reflective screen provides a clear glare free viewing experience for Mid-day viewing with 178 degree viewing angle that allows you to see the picture clear from virtually anywhere in the room. The QM9K is also a beast when it comes to video games as well. The 144hz refresh rate and built in AMD processor taking it to 288 ensures minimal lag and high kill rates for you COD fans out there. I was blown away the first time I booted up the new COD. The realism in the textures and visuals was insane. The minimal screen tears and just fluidity of how the Q9K handles fast moving objects is impressive. Even my wife who usually isn’t interested in video games couldn’t get over how good the TV looked. You pair that experience with the built in Bang and Olufsen speakers and you have an immersive TV that delivers on all levels. The speakers are a nice bonus as the TV can double as a Bluetooth speaker when not in use. Overall, I am very pleased with the TCL QM9K Mini-LED TV. It blows away our current family room tv in every way shape or form. If you’re looking for a TV with all the features you could ever want or need for the next 5-10 years, the QM9K is it. It’s a powerhouse of a TV, plain and simple! ||| review18 - Great tv, tcl has come a long way ! It’s intended as a direct competition to the top-tier Mini-LED and OLED models. It even sits above the already high-performing QM8K. I believe there's another model that is considered the "flagship," but I really don't see how the QM9K is not it. It offers an increase in hardware capabilities and overall horsepower. Plus, the QM9K is special because it has features like built-in Google Gemini.The TV has a cool room sensor built-in that can tell if someone's actually in the room. This means it can automatically switch to a nice ambient art mode or just power down to save some electricity. The feature works very well. The QM9K is an extremely bright TV with a TCL-rating up to 6,500 nits of peak brightness. I’ve watched video reviews where real-world HDR measurements in a 10% window showed it hitting between 4,200 and 4,400 nits, making it one of the brightest consumer TVs available. These measurements were taken in a small area of the screen, which is more telling of the limitations of these types of tests. Though this TV was shown to be capable of maintaining over 800 nits full-screen. The W-HVA panel improves off-angle viewing compared to previous generations of LCD or LED but still doesn’t compare to my OLED. It's supposed to have an industry-leading number of dimming zones, up to 6,000. I noticed very little blooming, but a little was still there before a firmware update that helped. I was very impressed by color accuracy and blacks in SDR Filmmaker Mode right out of the box. HDR Filmmaker was also just as good. I really liked their Movie mode as well. It supports all major HDR formats, including Dolby Vision IQ, HDR10+, HDR10, HLG, and IMAX Enhanced. Watching movies at night felt like being in my own theater (and I saved $20+ a person in the process). The TV runs the latest version of Google TV and includes the Gemini AI Assistant built in. It’s the snappiest version of Google TV or Android TV I’ve used including Google’s OEM devices. I don’t think it's the quickest TV operating system but it's the best version of Google TV I’ve used. I wish the OS was more light weight and had less advertisements but that’s not necessarily on TCL. That’s my opinion of Google TV overall. The TV is modern looking, and TCL claims a zero-borderless design. It’s not quite borderless but the border is extremely thin. It’s the same border width as my two-year-old OLED. The slimmer bezel really does make a premium viewing experience. It almost fades into the wall. Included is a high-quality, backlit remote. I wish it came with number keys as it would make typing passcodes and passwords much easier. An ATSC 3.0 tuner is built-in for next-generation over-the-air broadcasts. I have not tried the tuner as the majority of my viewing is via streaming apps. Number keys on the remote would have made antenna channel surfing easier as well. It offers excellent gaming specifications, including support for 4K at 144Hz and up to 1080p at 288Hz. This is most definitely a great gaming TV. Includes HDMI 2.1 bandwidth on two ports, VRR support, and super low input lag. Though the motion handling could use improvement. I noticed some motion blur when I played Cyberpunk 2077. Honestly, the built-in sound on this TV is probably the best I've heard. They teamed up with Bang & Olufsen on the design, and it handles both Dolby Atmos and DTS:X. That said, it's a pretty slim TV, so you still need to be realistic about how loud and deep the audio can be. You will need to invest in a high quality soundbar, powered speakers, or a home theater system you want the whole home theater experience. While the TCL QM9K has great hardware, I’ve read about and seen videos about small problems with the aggressive brightness limiter, which to preserve colors, it can make the bright scenes too dim. In the daytime I sometimes choose to turn off auto brightness during sports and some movies to get brighter in my family room with many windows. Also, read some buyers and reviewers seeing problems with loss of fine shadow details and overblown highlights. Everything the QM8K did so well, the QM9K is a little better. As amazing of an image and colors are on the QM9K, the QM8K is going to a better value for the average consumer.

Beautiful picture and sound . Geek Squad was fantastic. ||| review3 - Let’s get to the point. If you're looking for a high-end top of the line TV that pushes the envelope on clarity, brightness, sound quality and smart features, you should consider the TCL QM9K 65 inch. My previous TV was the Vizio M Series 50 inch that I’ve had since 2019. It was and still is a great TV but I thought it was time for an upgrade to see what has changed over the last several years with TV’s, so enter the QM9k. Inside the box came the TV( well protected), the usual paperwork, the stand with necessary screws, cable management clips, the remote( with 2 AAA batteries). Attaching the stand, swapping HDMI cables and placing the TV didn’t take long( ~20 mins) especially if you have two people working on it. You can also mount it if needed but you’ll need the required tools, and likely expertise to get it done properly for your setup. Once powered on you’ll have to go through a few rounds of initial setup options and updates, (it is a smart tv after all), especially if you’re a Google account holder and want to attach your account. This took me around 20~30 mins. I won’t do a spec dumb since that’s easily found on the BestBuy’s page for the QM9K but I will share what I liked. The first thing that struck me was how bright it was. According to TCL it can achieve 6500 nits. This was actually pretty great for me given that my living room gets flushed with a tonne of natural light during the day and based on where I’ve placed the tv the glare would lead me to pull the curtains. But those days are gone, my curtains can now be pulled all day without sunlight affecting my viewing experience. The next thing I noticed was that the screen is near bezel less and it had great viewing angles. When it comes to viewing content, this TV is top notch, especially if you are viewing a lot of HDR content. “Colors pop” would be an understatement , they explode whether you are watching films, sports or gaming. On the topic of gaming this excels! This was set up with my PS5 and no matter what I threw at it, a shooter like The Finals, sports like Fifa or more story driven like Ghost of Yotei (currently playing & loving this) it crushed it. I don’t even know what lag is anymore. Not to forget audio, but the sound from the Bang and Olufsen speakers was definitely an improvement from my previous tv. It is very good but you won’t be getting theater-sounding performance without pairing it with a dedicated sound system, which you can attach either via the HDMI eARC port or through blutooth. The bottom line is you can’t go wrong with the QM9K, you’re getting outstanding performance in many areas and you’ll never wanna look away. ||| review4 - Regarding setup and unboxing the 65 inch TCL QM9K, I am a fairly big guy (6'2") and I was able to set it up by myself although the instructions don't recommend that. The base has two levels you can set it at, one of which is higher in case you have a soundbar which we do. The base/stand provides a convenient area to place our soundbar on. However, it cannot be set back flush with the TV, if it is it will block the sensor on the lower front of the TV so I had to place the soundbar several inches in front of it. Once powered on, the TV will guide you through setting it up which includes logging into your Google account (this is our first Google TV) and that actually goes pretty smoothly in conjunction with your phone. Added bonus, I now have Google Home on my TV so I can change my thermostat or view our security cameras from my television, pretty cool. Our living room has a "cut out" in the wall as was the style of some home builders back in the late 90’s/early 2000's, the intent of which was to recess your TV back into the cutout so its flush with the fireplace. Well, that doesn't really work these days with larger TV screens so ours sits in front of the cutout (see picture). This affects the rear-facing speakers and kind of mutes them. While the Bang and Olufsen speakers are the best sounding built-in TV speakers I've ever heard along with impressive deep bass for such a thin TV, they don't work as good as our front-facing soundbar and subwoofer. According to TCL the screen "features an anti-reflective screen treatment that reduces mirror-like reflections from windows and overhead lights" and this matters in our living room. We have 8 big picture windows which allow tons of light through our living room and its been a problem with previous TVs. But the TCL QM9K has eliminated that, we get no reflections or glaring from our windows anymore. So here's how our TV setup works: we pay for DirecTV service at our cabin up in the Rocky Mountains and we use DirecTV Stream down at our main home since its included with the service. Our previous smart TV did not allow the DirecTV Stream app to be loaded so we had to use a streaming device, in our case a Roku Ultra. When I first setup the TCL QM9K I also connected the Roku Ultra just by default assuming I'd need it. Turns out the DirecTV Stream app is compatible with Google TV so that is convenient. But more importantly, I compared the picture using both methods and the difference is significant. When I first tested this viewing through the Roku Ultra the picture is great, but when viewing directly through the TCL it becomes phenomenal. It is stunningly crystal clear with bright gorgeous colors and deep blacks. When I'd switch back through the Roku Ultra the picture looks duller, more pixelated and the colors are muted. Switching back to viewing through the TCL the picture just comes alive. It is so good it looks almost like 3D, I was amazed at the difference. I also compared the pictures for viewing through the TCL vs Roku for other streaming apps like Netflix and found the differences to be less dramatic with the nod being given to the TCL as it always seemed brighter and clearer but the differences weren't huge, not like the case for the DirecTV Stream app. So to sum this up, the TCL has eliminated the need for our Roku and the picture is simply incredible. Regarding the Ambient Display, I like the idea. Per TCL's description: "With the Ambient Mode Sensor, the TCL QM9K detects your presence and responds. Enter the room and the screen lights up with a clean screensaver or helpful widgets you choose. Step away and it shuts off to save energy and reduce distractions." I have checked and doublechecked all the settings, read and re-read the user guide, searched the internet, watch videos, etc., to ensure its active and setup correctly but I just can't make it work. It has never turned on or off as described and I'm positive my soundbar isn't blocking the ambient sensor but it just does not work as expected. Then this morning as my wife was watching the TV it just shut off without warning. So I’m thinking its user error and I’ve setup something incorrectly in the ambient display settings but it doesn’t matter since my wife asked me to turn off that function and we’ll just stick with old school and use the remote power button. Speaking of the remote, its backlit which I love and works great. For example, using our old Roku remote you’d have to point it directly at the soundbar to adjust the volume as it uses infrared (IR). With the TCL remote that’s not necessary as it uses radio frequency (RF) to adjust volume and that works way better. I also love the screensaver which I configured to my Google Photos. I could sit there and watch it for hours viewing photos I haven't seen in years. However, the screensaver has never actually gone into 'screensaver mode' when I’ve had the TV on. I have had to turn it on manually with a quick click of the power button. I’ve tested it numerous times by leaving the TV idle but it has never come on based on my Screensaver settings. Then last night while my wife was watching a movie and said she got a message from the TV a couple of times saying the screensaver was about to turn on. She had to override that message a few times which was kind of annoying during the movie so I think this is related to my inability to make the ambient display work properly. Pretty sure its user error as I’m still trying to figure that out and why it doesn't seem to work as described. I am certainly not knocking off any stars in my review for that as this is one awesome television with the best picture I have ever seen, a rich feature set that's easy to use and dial it in as I like, and excellent sound (even though I prefer my soundbar). Five stars, no doubt about it. ||| review5 - My previous TVs have all been budget brand. They were great, but they are not even in the same universe as the TCL QM9K. I also watched during the day and with two windows across from the TV and the sun hitting them, it was still bright and easy to see. I have always had a soundbar for my living room TV, but with these speakers, I don't think I will be getting a soundbar. The sound is loud, clear and deep. Does a great job. ||| review16 - [Employee of bestbuy] So far the tv is excellent with great picture and sound! ||| review17 - TCL has been an emerging TV powerhouse in the US market since 2013 and is now the fastest growing TV brand in America. This TV is by far one of the best I’ve ever tested and should seriously be on your short list of considerations if you’re in the market. Initial unboxing of the tv was easy and straight forward. We had the stand on in less than a few minutes and were rocking and ready to go. First impressions of the tv itself is it feels very high end. The minimal frame on the outside of the tv compared to our old family room Samsung is a nice change. The tv isn’t overly heavy for a 65 inch and will be easy to mount over the fireplace once I get some help installing this weekend. Just wish they had put the Power Button on the top left corner, I’ve inadvertently muted my TV a few times now because they put the power button on the right side, but I’ll adjust! Setup with Google TV is as seamless a process as you’ll find. I love the Google UI and the ability to pre-load your favorite apps. Coming from a 7-year-old Samsung in our main living room area it’s strikingly apparent how old, outdated and basic the software was. Google TV feels like a whole new TV experience, especially with the introduction of AI and Gemini. Gemini is just scratching the surface of capabilities. Some of the highlights are you can use it to answer debates among family members with detailed answers to questions. Point towards helpful YouTube videos to solve how to problems at home. It can recommend new shows based on preferences or even do season recaps of shows to help you catch up. It can even help you find a TV show by vaguely describing it like how Apple Music works with lyrics. Hands free access with “Hey Google” is possible as well as well as automation of Google Home devices connected to your home network. My favorite feature so far is the ability to have it detect when someone enters the room and turn on to standby mode which will either display art or photos loaded to your Google Account. There are also additional widgets that can display weather, news, as well. The Technical Specs on this tv are impressive. If you’re considering this model you probably have done some homework already on features, so I won’t dive too deep into the technical aspects of this tv. The QM9K is also a beast when it comes to video games as well. The 144hz refresh rate and built in AMD processor taking it to 288 ensures minimal lag and high kill rates for you COD fans out there. I was blown away the first time I booted up the new COD. The realism in the textures and visuals was insane. The minimal screen tears and just fluidity of how the Q9K handles fast moving objects is impressive. Even my wife who usually isn’t interested in video games couldn’t get over how good the TV looked. You pair that experience with the built in Bang and Olufsen speakers and you have an immersive TV that delivers on all levels. The speakers are a nice bonus as the TV can double as a Bluetooth speaker when not in use. Overall, I am very pleased with the TCL QM9K Mini-LED TV. It blows away our current family room tv in every way shape or form. If you’re looking for a TV with all the features you could ever want or need for the next 5-10 years, the QM9K is it. It’s a powerhouse of a TV, plain and simple! ||| review18 - Great tv, tcl has come a long way ! It’s intended as a direct competition to the top-tier Mini-LED and OLED models. It even sits above the already high-performing QM8K. I believe there's another model that is considered the "flagship," but I really don't see how the QM9K is not it. It offers an increase in hardware capabilities and overall horsepower. Plus, the QM9K is special because it has features like built-in Google Gemini.The TV has a cool room sensor built-in that can tell if someone's actually in the room. This means it can automatically switch to a nice ambient art mode or just power down to save some electricity. The feature works very well. The QM9K is an extremely bright TV with a TCL-rating up to 6,500 nits of peak brightness. I’ve watched video reviews where real-world HDR measurements in a 10% window showed it hitting between 4,200 and 4,400 nits, making it one of the brightest consumer TVs available. These measurements were taken in a small area of the screen, which is more telling of the limitations of these types of tests. Though this TV was shown to be capable of maintaining over 800 nits full-screen. The W-HVA panel improves off-angle viewing compared to previous generations of LCD or LED but still doesn’t compare to my OLED. It's supposed to have an industry-leading number of dimming zones, up to 6,000. I noticed very little blooming, but a little was still there before a firmware update that helped. I was very impressed by color accuracy and blacks in SDR Filmmaker Mode right out of the box. HDR Filmmaker was also just as good. I really liked their Movie mode as well. It supports all major HDR formats, including Dolby Vision IQ, HDR10+, HDR10, HLG, and IMAX Enhanced. Watching movies at night felt like being in my own theater (and I saved $20+ a person in the process). The TV runs the latest version of Google TV and includes the Gemini AI Assistant built in. It’s the snappiest version of Google TV or Android TV I’ve used including Google’s OEM devices. I don’t think it's the quickest TV operating system but it's the best version of Google TV I’ve used. I wish the OS was more light weight and had less advertisements but that’s not necessarily on TCL. That’s my opinion of Google TV overall. The TV is modern looking, and TCL claims a zero-borderless design. It’s not quite borderless but the border is extremely thin. It’s the same border width as my two-year-old OLED. The slimmer bezel really does make a premium viewing experience. It almost fades into the wall. Included is a high-quality, backlit remote. I wish it came with number keys as it would make typing passcodes and passwords much easier. An ATSC 3.0 tuner is built-in for next-generation over-the-air broadcasts. I have not tried the tuner as the majority of my viewing is via streaming apps. Number keys on the remote would have made antenna channel surfing easier as well. It offers excellent gaming specifications, including support for 4K at 144Hz and up to 1080p at 288Hz. This is most definitely a great gaming TV. Includes HDMI 2.1 bandwidth on two ports, VRR support, and super low input lag. Though the motion handling could use improvement. I noticed some motion blur when I played Cyberpunk 2077. Honestly, the built-in sound on this TV is probably the best I've heard. They teamed up with Bang & Olufsen on the design, and it handles both Dolby Atmos and DTS:X. That said, it's a pretty slim TV, so you still need to be realistic about how loud and deep the audio can be. You will need to invest in a high quality soundbar, powered speakers, or a home theater system you want the whole home theater experience. While the TCL QM9K has great hardware, I’ve read about and seen videos about small problems with the aggressive brightness limiter, which to preserve colors, it can make the bright scenes too dim. In the daytime I sometimes choose to turn off auto brightness during sports and some movies to get brighter in my family room with many windows. Also, read some buyers and reviewers seeing problems with loss of fine shadow details and overblown highlights. Everything the QM8K did so well, the QM9K is a little better. As amazing of an image and colors are on the QM9K, the QM8K is going to a better value for the average consumer.

column8: review1 - The 2025 Hisense 65U75QG miniLED is perhaps the best display, dollar-for-dollar in its price range. Its 1,800 local dimming zones allow for it to produce very good black levels with incredible contrast. Its peak brightness is 3,000 nits, allowing it to easily overcome sunlight or reflections from other sources in your room. We have it on a tv stand in our living room, directly across from an entire wall of windows, and have had zero issues during any time of the day. The setup was easy, completed from our phone. The TV was connected via Google account within minutes. Native apps were download and updated, and we were quickly able to start enjoying our favorite streaming services. 4K 60FPS content streamed beautifully. I have included a screenshot showing a nearly 100Mbit per second video playing flawlessly. This is all done over wifi, quite a distance from the router, so I expect the vast majority of people will see similarly-excellent streaming quality. The built-in speakers are very clear, with no muddiness even at higher volumes. The sound easily fills the space of our 30x20 living room. I don't feel there is any need to attach a soundbar at this time, but might in the future. The controller is very easy to use, with dedicated buttons for many of the top streaming services. Just like the TV itself, it has high build quality, and feels good in your hand. It also looks very premium with is brushed metal face. We briefly connected our PC to try the 165Hz Game mode, and were very impressed with the smooth gaming at that frame rate. Prior to this, our 'best' TV was only capable of 120FPS, so this was a significant bump in performance. If your computer or console can play games at 165Hz/FPS, you owe it to yourself to try it out. I would highly recommend this TV to anyone looking for great build quality, loads of built-in features, excellent sound, and stunning picture quality typically only seen in much-more-expensive displays. Hisense has a winner on its hands with the 65U75QG. ||| review2 - I’ve had an OLED in my living room for a few months but, for my upstairs setup, I wanted a TV that could provide a brighter, more impactful image than a typical OLED’s 1000 nits ceiling. The color matched remote also feels premium, with backlit buttons and voice command support. You’re getting brightness levels and gaming chops typically reserved for flagship models that cost significantly more. While I could nitpick about minor haloing or response times, these are things you might not even notice with how exceptional the overall picture is. column18: review1 - The 2025 Hisense 65U75QG miniLED is perhaps the best display, dollar-for-dollar in its price range. Its 1,800 local dimming zones allow for it to produce very good black levels with incredible contrast. Its peak brightness is 3,000 nits, allowing it to easily overcome sunlight or reflections from other sources in your room. We have it on a tv stand in our living room, directly across from an entire wall of windows, and have had zero issues during any time of the day. The setup was easy, completed from our phone. The TV was connected via Google account within minutes. Native apps were download and updated, and we were quickly able to start enjoying our favorite streaming services. 4K 60FPS content streamed beautifully. I have included a screenshot showing a nearly 100Mbit per second video playing flawlessly. This is all done over wifi, quite a distance from the router, so I expect the vast majority of people will see similarly-excellent streaming quality. The built-in speakers are very clear, with no muddiness even at higher volumes. The sound easily fills the space of our 30x20 living room. I don't feel there is any need to attach a soundbar at this time, but might in the future. The controller is very easy to use, with dedicated buttons for many of the top streaming services. Just like the TV itself, it has high build quality, and feels good in your hand. It also looks very premium with is brushed metal face. We briefly connected our PC to try the 165Hz Game mode, and were very impressed with the smooth gaming at that frame rate. Prior to this, our 'best' TV was only capable of 120FPS, so this was a significant bump in performance. If your computer or console can play games at 165Hz/FPS, you owe it to yourself to try it out. I would highly recommend this TV to anyone looking for great build quality, loads of built-in features, excellent sound, and stunning picture quality typically only seen in much-more-expensive displays. Hisense has a winner on its hands with the 65U75QG. ||| review2 - I’ve had an OLED in my living room for a few months but, for my upstairs setup, I wanted a TV that could provide a brighter, more impactful image than a typical OLED’s 1000 nits ceiling. It has two stand legs that screw into the bottom and a decorative cover that slides between them, providing the TV a refined polished metal accent. The color matched remote also feels premium, with backlit buttons and voice command support. The built-in speakers, a 50W 2.1.2 channel system, punch well above their weight and even support Dolby Atmos. When scrolling through the menu or switching inputs, the Google TV OS felt snappy. Even high-bitrate 4K redux streams played without any hiccups. This thing can get eye-searingly bright, with highlights approaching 3000 nits. The quantum dot display means that colors pop off the screen and the mini-LED backlight does a great job of delivering deep blacks with minimal blooming. I noticed some minor haloing around subtitles in pitch-black scenes in a dark viewing environment. The display also handles reflections and ambient light quite well, with no loss of shadow detail in bright rooms. Viewing angles are typical of a VA panel, with image degradation kicking in about 35 degrees off-axis, which is fine for a couch setup. Straight out of the box, I found that the Standard picture preset with Warm 2 color temperature provides a great starting point to tinker with the full suite of image settings to get the picture looking exactly how you want it. Its gaming performance is the other big standout. All four HDMI 2.1 ports on the TV support both 4K 165Hz and 1080p 288Hz with VRR. There’s practically no input lag, but I feel the pixel response times could be a bit faster - dark scenes in horror games like Resident Evil can have some black smearing in fast motion. Still, gameplay in fast-paced titles like Apex Legends always felt fluid and responsive, and I never felt like I could blame the TV for any of my shortcomings. This thing is the real deal. You’re getting brightness levels and gaming chops typically reserved for flagship models that cost significantly more. While I could nitpick about minor haloing or response times, these are things you might not even notice with how exceptional the overall picture is. column8: review1 - We went from a 65 Sony A80J OLED to this and the TCL is better. I honestly can’t believe it. After spending years with OLED I was convinced I would always need OLEDS in my home. Being generally unhappy with the performance of the X90K with a handful of dimming zones I was skeptical about this QM6K, but after carefully studying the performance of each TV the number reported from Rtings.com indicated that the QM6K was at least 2x better in quite a few places than my beloved A80J. And at a quarter of the cost I needed to see it for myself. I did, I barely needed to even change any settings something I’ve been used to doing with almost every Sony I’ve purchased over years. This is my first non Sony TV I’ve bought and kept. The short of it. The Q6MK was significantly brighter than my A80J in real life and I think even better than what was reported by rtings.com. I cant’t even believe the black levels I am seeing its basically OLED good or in worst cases 95% as good. Me and my family are all the abovers when it comes to uses gaming, movies, TV. My wife is going on strikes in Apex 120hz on the PS5 is epic, CoD 2019 was tested went a few rounds at 120 fps no problem. There is an fps counter in a gaming menu that tells you what fps you are running. Which is amazing. My other tvs could do this too but the input lag was noticeably lower on the QM6K. We are talking milliseconds faster here. But if you are playing cod with these new ai finger robot kids these days, every millisecond counts. We’ve watched all of Alien Earth on the new set and I went back and tested all the movies I know in and out. I can actually tell which movies were mastered in HDR and which were not. Even those that were not looked better than they ever did on my embarrassingly dim A80J. The QM6K is almost 2x as bright as my X90K, which is reported to be brighter than the QM6K but its NOT, not even close actually. The youtuber reviews from the main guys seem to think this tv isn’t hitting but it HITS! If I were to complain about anything it’s been the performance of the remote. Initially it was very slow and seemed like the tv wasn’t responding correctly. But I unpaired the remote and just used the RF and it went back being snappy and very fast. But then I paired it with bluetooth again and it started being slow again. i dealt with this for about 1 week then the remote just randomly started working okay and I haven’t thought about it til now. The remote is backlit and tells you how much battery life you have left in the aaa in the settings. The backlit remote is the best thing ever. If would have spent double and got a A95j or X95K I would have experienced the backlit remote earlier but after having it on the QM6K it was one of the best upgrades I got. I always loved Sony because of how perfectly you could dial in the motion. They have some super complex menus that really let you tailor the motion smoothing (interpolation) how you want. They were the best for as long as I can remember. And it was my biggest fear that the TCL wouldn’t be good enough. Sigh* this Q6MK is better, its just easier to dial in, and does everything the best Sony tv ever did. I could careless what a Bravia 7 or 9 is doing right now. Sony would have loved that I pay 2K for a Bravia 8 II. I honestly can’t justify these high end OLED and halo mini LED when Mid range mini LED TVs are better than top tier models from 3 years ago its wild. Spec wise and past experience is telling me I should have gotten the Sony Bravia 8 II. After getting this TCL. Sony is gonna have a hard time selling me anything ever again. I’ll get the QM9K unless Sony gets their act together on price point. ||| review2 - Once you get your settings dialed in this thing is a beauty. Super bright and close to oled blacks. Bery colorful and the refresh rate is amazing! ||| review3 - The TCL 65" QM6K Mini-LED TV (2025) offers stunning 4K picture quality with impressive brightness, deep contrast, and vivid colors thanks to its QD Mini-LED display and local dimming technology. It delivers smooth motion and vibrant HDR performance, making movies, sports, and gaming look exceptional. Overall, the TCL QM6K is a great value—combining premium-level performance and smart features at a very reasonable price. ||| review4 - I never owned a TCL tv until a few years ago when i bought one for my bedroom. column8: review1 - I work as a facility manager at a high school, so I am used to lifting heavy equipment and installing a TV, but getting this 85-inch TV set up in my home was definitely a two-person job. The metal feet feel sturdy enough and have a nice spot in the back to tuck the wires away, which keeps the install looking clean. Once we turned it on, the first thing my girlfriend and I noticed was the brightness. It gets incredibly bright, making colors look vibrant and punchy. While the blacks are deep, I did notice some light blooming around subtitles in dark movie scenes. The sound is surprisingly good enough, and I haven't hooked up a soundbar yet because the built-in subwoofer has decent bass. I really like that all four inputs on the back are high-speed HDMI 2.1 ports. I have 2 gaming consoles, and this makes switching between them easy, without moving cords around to get the benefits of HDMI 2.1. The remote lights up, which is handy at night. I got it during Black Friday; the value is hard to beat for a screen this size at that price. I took off a star because the screen handles reflections poorly if a lamp is on, and fast motion can look a bit blurry. ||| review2 - The Hisense 85U75QG is a great gaming TV for anyone who wants a huge screen paired with bright HDR+, vibrant color, and console support. Setup was a breeze. With the QR code setup with the Google TV account connected to your google account it logged you into most things and sets up Google TV instantly. Dolby Atmos and the 2.1.2 multi-channel surround sound it immerses you in sound like a movie theater but at home or on set of a film! My brother thought I had a soundbar connected to the TV. The native refresh rate panel up to 165 Hz has changed my gaming, with The AMD Freesync Premium Pro and Low latency mode, it makes sure I am never late and I don't miss anything or movement in the shot. AI Upscaling has been amazing with connecting it to my gaming console, the fast paced fighting scenes and with clarity even while in motion, I can see every since detail of the action. Full sound, decent bass, clear. The picture quality is really good for this size seen up close. The color looks quite natural. The TV was set to Warm1 temperature and Dolby Vision IQ. I changed Warm1 to Standard which looked a tad better to me. Several items like local dimming were currently unavailable to adjust, and I will dive in further to settings when fine tuning. Action scenes were clean, and I could not identify any motion blur or stuttering. The blacks are much better than I expected, and didn't see much, if any, blooming. Doing this review basically out-of-the-box, I am really impressed with this Hisense TV. There are plenty of settings to enhance color, brightness, etc. From where I sit, I am happy just as it is, if I choose to be lazy. For an 85" MiniLED TV, I feel this is a great value. column8: review1 - Hisense 85" Mini Led Fire TV First thought, this TV is BIG and heavy. You will need two people to move it around. After unboxing and installing the stand brackets (very simple to install and easily removed for a wall bracket) we moved it onto a credenza for a temporary home. The width of the stand brackets is 62" wide. The initial setup - Plug in your input source into one of 4 HDMI inputs, attach the power plug and follow the simple on screen instructions to continue the easy setup. Very quick and easy, after a short 5 min software update you are ready to go. The initial burst of color on the massive 85" inch is extraordinary. The colors were bright and the black was very deep with terrific contrast. The initial screen of the company logo looked great and led to the onscreen setup of the Fire TV operating system. At this point my focus shifted to the small compact remote control. Very simple and easily learned. You can do most things by using Alexa and voice commands. You can of course do it the old fashion way by using the manual control buttons. There are only 14 buttons not including the 4 direct streaming channels, Prime, Netflix, Disney and Amazon Music. If you are only streaming, you can download and install all of the standard big streamers or choose from hundreds of other channels. To switch back to cable input, I found 3 ways to switch back to HDMI input so far, very intuitive. The basic sound is very good, I have not yet hooked it up to my home theater yet. The wireless or wired hookup to the internet is also very simple and intuitive' The included Quick Setup Guide is a fast read and very easy to understand. The operating system really does almost everything on its own. Finally, the picture is better than the expensive brand I am replacing. The Mini Leds seem to make a much more attractive picture than I had ever seen before. The details are amazingly clear and sharp. I will eventually be putting this up on a wall bracket soon, but for now I am enjoying the best large screen TV I have ever had. My know it all kids fully agree! ||| review2 - I’m seriously blown away by the Hisense 85U65QF. This 85" Mini-LED looks incredible mounted above my fireplace and delivers an amazingly clean, vibrant picture. Dolby Vision and Dolby Vision IQ look fantastic straight out of the box—no calibration needed whatsoever. Even my Apple TV confirms Dolby Vision doesn’t need any tweaks, and I completely agree. The picture quality is outstanding with deep, inky blacks, almost no glare thanks to the near-matte screen finish, and excellent off-angle viewing. Honestly, I can’t tell much of a difference between this and my OLEDs, which is saying a lot. The built-in Dolby Atmos audio also sounds surprisingly great and easily fills the room. The only minor downside is that eARC is limited to HDMI port 1, which tops out at 60Hz instead of 144Hz. It’s not an issue for sound, but it can be inconvenient if you’re using a receiver. Overall, this TV massively exceeds expectations and feels like a premium, plug-and-play experience. I couldn’t be happier with it. ||| review3 - The Hisense 85” U6 Series Mini-LED QLED absolutely exceeded my expectations, especially when it comes to image quality. For a screen this large, clarity is everything, and Hisense nailed it. The contrast is especially impressive and motion is smooth, crisp, and clean. The Filmmaker Mode is a huge highlight, making you feel like you’re in the movie theater. Setting up the Fire TV was as easy as logging into my Amazon account and navigation is a breeze. I especially love having all apps and movie recommendations in the main screen, so there’s no going to different menus to search for new content to watch. Overall, this TV delivers premium level picture quality without the premium price tag. If you want a giant screen with beautiful color, excellent contrast, and seriously impressive HDR performance, the Hisense 85U65QF is a phenomenal choice. ||| review4 - This TV delivered way more than I was expecting. The picture quality is the first thing that stands out. The mini leds really make it look sharp and vibrant. The dark scenes actually look black instead of grey and the colors pop without looking overdone. This TV makes watching movies and sports like a theater experience. The game mode on it also works flawlessly I saw no input lag while gaming. The built in fire tv interface is very convenient and all the streaming apps are already there. It's very simple to navigate and you get tons extra features also. The sound on this TV is exceptional I never had to really then it up that high. Overall this TV is great. It's bright, clear, huge and easy to set up. If you want a big TV with good quality picture then this is an easy recommendation. ||| review5 - The Hisense 85" U6 Series offers an impressive blend of picture quality, smart features, and sound performance in a massive screen format. Its Mini-LED and QLED technology delivers vibrant colors, deep contrast, and sharp 4K resolution, making movies and games visually stunning. Integrated Fire TV provides seamless access to streaming apps, and Alexa voice control adds hands-free convenience for navigation and smart home integration. Sound quality is clear and immersive with Dolby Atmos support, though a soundbar may enhance bass for audiophiles. While the TV excels in front-facing viewing, its VA panel limits wide-angle visibility, making it best suited for central seating arrangements. Overall, it’s a fantastic choice for home theater enthusiasts seeking a smart, high-performance 85" display. This television makes for a great day watching football and having friends over for movie night. ||| review6 - I upgraded to the Hisense 85″ U65QF and have been very happy with it so far. The picture quality is much better than I expected for the price, with bright colors and good contrast. It holds up well in a bright family room and doesn’t look washed out during the day. Sports and movies look smooth, and HDR content really pops. Setup was easy and the Fire TV interface is straightforward to use. The sound is decent, though a soundbar helps. Overall, it feels like a great value for a large, modern TV. Loved the Fire Tv integration to get to the apps quickly. I would highly recommend the upgrade especially if you have a LED tv. ||| review7 - Bought this for my bedroom and it is a monster of a tv. It truly feels like an in-home cinema. Setup was easy however I did have an issue. My remote did not want to connect to the tv. The remote was able to control the volume, power, and directional buttons but the TV was stuck on “tap the home button to sync remote”. I had to spend about 20 minutes figuring out how to pair, including unmounting the tv and plugging in my router via Ethernet so the tv could receive an update and be able to connect to the remote. I saw some people suggest resetting the remote via home, menu, and left button but that didn’t work. Others said to disconnect the tv but that didn’t work either. Apart from that, my other issue is how sensitive the light sensor is. There’s a feature that allows the tv to adjust its brightness based on the light in the room. I found it being much to sudden in a controlled dark room. The tv would dim based on the brightness of its own screen. These two things are small nits of the tv which are both easily fixable. I never had another issue with the remote and turning off auto brightness fixed the second issue. The picture is fantastic, the sound is amazing and my walls shake from the bass and strength of the speakers. It’s also extremely bright. This would no doubt do great in rooms that get a lot of light. The refresh rate is also amazing. I use the tv for gaming and have absolutely no issues with the frame rate. It truly is a tv that can handle all. ||| review8 - This is our second Hisense TV—both U6 models, just different sizes. That should tell you something right there. I had three hard requirements when shopping: solid price, full array local dimming, and good RTings.com ratings. Honestly, that narrowed it down to basically one option—the Hisense U6. The U7 doesn't justify the extra cost, and anything cheaper just doesn't have what you actually need. Simple as that. Full array local dimming that actually makes a difference in contrast and shadow detail. eARC/ARC so you can hook up better audio without hassle (I'm not about to use optical with my soundbar and I'll give up an HDMI port). 144Hz refresh rate (which I'll probably never use, but hey, nice to have if you're into gaming). Dolby Vision support for that extra pop. QLED color tech that handles the details right. And here's the kicker—it comes with a 2 year warranty, which is basically unheard of in TVs these days. I could do without any AI features, but I will at least give them a try once everything is calibrated. We're not going to use the Fire TV part at all, that's just not our setup. But if you're already in the Alexa/Amazon ecosystem, having it built in is actually convenient. One less device cluttering your entertainment center. It's a straightforward choice if you know what matters and don't want to overpay for features you'll never touch. Does exactly what it's supposed to do without the BS markup. column5: TCL - 85" Class QM6K Series 4K UHD HDR QD Mini LED Smart TV with Google TV (2025)
column8: review1 - We don’t have any regrets with this TCL TV. The size works well for our space and feels immersive without being excessive. The matte screen finish is especially useful and does a great job reducing glare in our bright living room. We chose this Mini-LED over an OLED because it handles bright rooms better, and in our situation it also made more sense from a pricing standpoint. For an 86-inch TV, it delivers strong picture quality without feeling like a compromise. The image looks sharp, colors are vibrant, contrast is good, and the TV gets bright without looking washed out. The interface is responsive and easy to navigate. Sound quality exceeded our expectations and has been enough that we haven’t felt an immediate need to add a soundbar. The remote is well designed. It feels sturdy while still being compact, and it’s more reliable than remotes we’ve used with higher priced TVs. The app-based remote also works well and is fast and responsive. We had seen some mixed opinions about TCL beforehand, so we opted for a 5-year warranty for peace of mind. So far, everything has been working as expected. Friends and family who have seen the TV in person are often surprised by how good it looks, and we’ve been asked more than once what model it is. This is a very large and heavy TV. We originally paid for delivery and professional installation, but with how Best Buy handled the delivery and install process, we ended up having to pick it up ourselves. It barely fit in a Tundra truck bed. Professional installation was still helpful given the size, though the coordination required more follow-up than expected. None of this reflects on the TV itself, but it’s something you may want to keep in mind if adding these extra services at checkout. We’ve run into a few minor issues specifically with YouTube Kids, but nothing that points to a problem with the TV itself. Overall, this was a solid choice for a large TV in a bright room, especially considering the size and price. ||| review2 - Overall this TV knocks it out of the park. Purchased this sight unseen due to it being so new. Online reviews gave me all the insight I needed. Best aspect is the mat screen. It cannot be understated how effectively this reduces reflective light. This is great for bright rooms. My living room has 10’ windows all around and this feature alone made this set far better than a brighter set. The second is the brightness doesn’t have to be eye scorching, to get a great picture. Ours is set lower and the auto settings allows it to slowly adjust throughout the day, so at night, you don’t suffer from eye fatigue. Colors seem slightly off so I turned off Dynamic color, which seemed to correct the issues. Local dimming is the way to go, getting the best that micro-LED can offer without the expense of OLED. Off axis is really good as well, due to newly designed LED lenses. Sound is good- if you adjust it, you can hear details and vocals but I’d suggest a sound bar. We paired ours with the Klipsch Core 210 and aren’t disappointed. Remote is very easy to operate and has background lit buttons, for easier navigation in the dark. Packaging is really well done. Only wish manufacturers would make it easier to attack the wall mount brackets, while still suspended in the styrofoam base. When unpacking, make sure to find and remove the metal feet up top, to avoid them falling and potentially damaging your TV or floor. They look very sturdy and have two mount points (wide and narrow). They come with mounting hardware as well. We didn’t use them and opted for a wall mount. Set weighs around 73 pounds, so make sure you have a helper. Hope this helps some of you. We purchased this during Memorial Day weekend and paid $1199, which was cheaper than a lot of older versions for sale. You can’t go wrong with this TV. My cats are mesmerized by it. ||| review3 - The price to performance and specs is truly unmatched.
