column8: review1 - I have a 77" OLED and a few 65" TVs and this 85" is in a totally different class in terms of size, so HAVE A PLAN before this thing arrives. You will need a big space to store the TV box (about 8' long and the size of a dinner table), 1' wide and heavy around 200lbs with all the packaging. Two able-bodied adults can pick it up by the side handles and move it but it is heavy. The freight delivery person and I were able to comfortable move the TV inside my foyer, and I had a friend help me take it out of the box and mount it. Also, if you plan to get a TV mount, make sure you pick a sturdy one with lag bolts that is wide enough to support 600mmx400mm VESA mounting brackets. Many smaller TVs are 400x400, but this TV is 600x400. The mount I used the Sanus Elite BLL2-B1 works well, however, it is JUST wide enough so that they is very little side to side tolerance, so you will want to make sure you measure and center up the TV how you like. The TV weighs 95lbs without the box. I was able to mount the wall mount by myself while it was in the box, take the measurements for the wall mount and then accurately measure and hang the mount frame on the wall using lag bolts. Two able bodied adults should be able to lift the TV on the wall, however a 3rd person supporting the weight in the middle may be needed. Also, plan your cables and power connectors before you mount everything up because you will not want to take this down later. Now on to the TV. It is absolutely stunning in terms of BRIGHTNESS. It advertises peak 3000 nits and honestly, it might hit it. I have a 77" QD-OLED TV and at 800-1000nits, this U7SG looks like the Sun compared to it. It is shockingly bright. No issues in full sunlight and in dark rooms and dark scenes, it will light up the room. The trade-off is blacks, while the full array local dimming and Hi-QLED MiniLED display, this display is still very good when it comes to black levels. Colors are absolutely stunning, you are going to have your jaw drop in any bright, animated or CGI moves. Motion is excellent, you also don't get the absolute pixel response times (this impacts how crisp images look in motion) as OLED, but 165Hz is fantastic and fast moving action movies and sports have no issues keeping up. Hockey, NASCAR, Soccer, all look amazing with no issues on this TV at all. I can't wait to see what the World Cup looks like on this TV. The green pitch will feel like you are in the game. I did some limited gaming from my laptop which has a 5080 mobile, however, this is slower than a desktop 5070 and really isn't suitable for a 4K display. I have a 5090 desktop, but I didn't get a chance to move it closer to my TV. Still, using the 5080 laptop showed what this display is capable of. I was able to get the full advertised 165Hz refresh with HDR and FreeSync Premium Pro (G-Sync compatible), but the colors looked more washed out and dimmer in Game Mode. There are a bunch of game mode settings which are nice, but I need to play with this more to get the HDR pop I am expecting that I got from my OLED and older Hisense. The built-in Google TV and Hisense processor was a real surprise. I've been using Apple TVs for years to avoid the built-in OSes and because the processors in the TVs are generally much slower or get bogged down quickly by the increasing demands of bloated apps. But this TV and Google TV are really snappy and responsive with apps loading quickly and supporting all of the high-end outputs like Dolby Vision and Atmos. I also really enjoy the remote. I wasn't sure at first given it is so big, but my kids really like it too. They love the texture of the dpad being metal with ridged rings and the feel and clickiness are perfect. They noticed right away how it had shortcut buttons for their favorite apps and its big enough to not lose easily unlike my Apple TV remote, but if it does get stuck in a couch cushion, you can hit a button on the TV which makes the remote emit a sound so you can find it easier. Great feature! Google TV has some cool features and the tool tips show you how to use it, like holding the confirm button to go back to your last channel or app, holding up for stats in games etc. This TV also supports Dolby Vision and HDR10+ natively, which is great since my OLED did not support Dolby Vision which is super annoying. The sound quality from the 2.1.2 speakers tuned by Devialet are also excellent for built-in TV speakers, however, I found they sounded a bit muddled likely due to their close proximity to the wall, so I opted to connect it to an LG Soundbar. This was another negative for this TV that appears to be common with Hisense TVs when connected via eARC to a soundbar. You have HDMI-CEC which allows you to control volume to the soundbar and you get a graphic showing volume + or -, however, it does not show the actual volume level on the screen like I get with Apple TV and other TVs. The TV does wake up my LG S95TR soundbar which did not work correctly with my 77" QD-OLED. I had to use a workaround on my OLED with Apple TV to deal with this, but eARC works perfectly on this TV. Build quality on the TV overall is excellent. It is thin for such a massive TV and the back is flat. There is also a MATTE coating on the screen to limit glare, but this does not negatively impact image quality at all. My wall is now literally a TV and my kids absolutely love it. They spent the entire weekend watching movies and asking for popcorn because 85" and sitting 4-5' closer than in my family room, really changes the level of immersiveness and gives us the BIG SCREEN experience at home. Now we are planning to change what was once our play room into a BIG SCREEN room and we'll hook up the Switch 2 and PS5 to it as well. Can't wait for the World Cup on this TV!!!! ||| review2 - The Hisense 85” TV is an absolutely breathtaking display that has completely reinvented my living room. We recently purchased a new house, and our existing 65” TV had become an eyesore because of the room layout. This room has an 11’ wall with an 18’ ceiling, along with upper and lower windows on the adjacent wall. As a result, our 65” TV setup was nearly unusable during peak daylight, not to mention significantly undersized for the space. Enter the Hisense 85” TV, which has changed everything. The panel claims a 3000 nits brightness, which puts it at the top end for Mini-LEDs. Based on all the stress tests I’ve run, I have no reason to question that claim. For reference, OLEDs generally top out around 1500 nits, and traditional LCDs around 1200 nits. In other words, this thing is ridiculously bright, which is exactly what you want when your living room is basically a sunroom like mine. A really interesting feature with this display is the native 165Hz panel, which leans heavily into gaming territory. I haven’t hooked it up to my PC yet to confirm a full 165Hz input, but I’d be very surprised if it didn’t support it, especially considering the four full HDMI 2.1 ports. Everything about this display suggests it’s built to handle high refresh rates and can pair with a PC. In terms of mounting this TV, there are a few things worth noting. I initially purchased a full motion mount because I assumed I’d need it to combat sunlight, but that turned out to be unnecessary. That said, I still recommend a mount that allows you to pull the TV away from the wall for access, because hanging this thing is a beast, and you don’t want to be taking it down once it’s up. Also, the mounting bracket position on the back of the TV sits much higher than expected. The top mounting holes measured around 38” from the bottom of the TV, which made me have to rethink my mounting strategy. In my case, that meant placing the wall bracket around 83” high so the TV would clear our 36” console we ordered, and still leave room for a soundbar. If you’re using the included stand, you have nothing to worry about in terms of stability. The stand base is literally a 1/4” sheet of iron that could likely stop a bullet. As for the display itself, this is probably the best panel I’ve ever seen, whether in-store or at home. The colors are stunning across the board, and I didn’t run into any issues in any of the display tests I tried. The anti-glare coating gives the TV a matte appearance when it’s off, but once it’s on, you’d swear it was glossy. More importantly, the anti-glare actually works. In one of my photos, you can see full sunlight is pouring through the windows, and there’s only a small reflection in the top corner of the screen. At night, the brightness of the TV literally changes the door of the room. One of my favorite features is the remote. I’m picky about remotes, to the point where I’ve avoided certain TVs because of them, and this remote has quickly become my favorite. It’s a great size, has some weight to it so it feels solid, the buttons are large and backlit, and best of all… it’s not pitch black. I can’t tell you how many times we’ve lost a black remote simply because it’s black and we can’t see it. On top of that, there’s a button under the TV that makes the remote beep if you can’t find it. It’s brilliant. I could honestly go on and on about this TV because I haven’t found a single weak spot. Everything just works the way it should. Even Google TV is fast and responsive, which hasn’t always been my experience on my other TVs. The built-in sound is also surprisingly good, as it has decent range and even manages a bit of bass. However, a TV this size deserves a proper sound system. I’ll be pairing it with my Sennheiser setup once our console arrives. If you have a bright room and are concerned about glare, this TV is absolutely the way to go. I was previously shopping OLEDs for this room because I didn’t want to sacrifice display quality; but couldn’t justify purchasing an OLED for a room like this, as they are better suited for low light. This Mini-LED panel gives me the quality without the sacrifice, and I could not be happier with it. ||| review3 - Hisense's 2026 85" inch Class U7 Series is impressive but it's the Mini-LED backlighting that sets this TV apart. The use of thousands of tiny LEDs ensures that it's really bright and really dark. The whites really shine (up to 3000 nits), but the blacks don't become soulless gray mush either. Whether it's a dark moment in a thriller or a sunny sports match, the TV performs well in both scenarios. Colors are also very good. The TV's QLED panel and Pantone certification means that colours don't appear too saturated. Skin tones look natural, greens don't look neon, and generally there's a good balance that gives everything, be it movies or sports, a more authentic look. The AI processing is also impressive, particularly when it comes to upscaling content from lower resolutions it won't turn everything into real 4K, but it does a good enough job to be noticeable. This is a gaming TV if ever there was one. The 165Hz refresh rate is particularly very impressive offering smooth motion and responsiveness particularly in gaming. The fact it has HDMI latest 2.1 inputs on all four ports means its well equipped for the latest consoles and gaming computers. Tools like the Game Bar allow quick and easy settings adjustments and this is no novelty. Overall it does a great job of motion while watching sports Quick camera moves, action scenes, and games are all clear with little blur, due to the MEMC (motion estimation and compensation) technology. Some film lovers might want to disable some of it for movies, but it's good to have the choice. Sound is surprisingly good for a flat-screen TV. The integrated 2.1.2 multi-channel system (tuned by Devialet) gives it a bit more of a punch. You can hear dialogue without trouble and there's a good sense of depth, particularly with Dolby Atmos. This isn't a replacement for a surround sound system, but it will do the trick for most homes and it can be complemented by a compatible soundbar to deliver more without a lot of effort. It has a modern design, with a thin, one piece backplate that doesn't interfere with the display. It's suitable for modern and more traditional decor alike. Other features, such as the anti-reflection coating, are also useful glare is minimal so it's not too hard to watch the TV during the day (great for a bright TV). Google TV remains one of the easiest to use smart TV systems. column18: review1 - I have a 77" OLED and a few 65" TVs and this 85" is in a totally different class in terms of size, so HAVE A PLAN before this thing arrives. You will need a big space to store the TV box (about 8' long and the size of a dinner table), 1' wide and heavy around 200lbs with all the packaging. Two able-bodied adults can pick it up by the side handles and move it but it is heavy. The freight delivery person and I were able to comfortable move the TV inside my foyer, and I had a friend help me take it out of the box and mount it. Also, if you plan to get a TV mount, make sure you pick a sturdy one with lag bolts that is wide enough to support 600mmx400mm VESA mounting brackets. Many smaller TVs are 400x400, but this TV is 600x400. The mount I used the Sanus Elite BLL2-B1 works well, however, it is JUST wide enough so that they is very little side to side tolerance, so you will want to make sure you measure and center up the TV how you like. The TV weighs 95lbs without the box. I was able to mount the wall mount by myself while it was in the box, take the measurements for the wall mount and then accurately measure and hang the mount frame on the wall using lag bolts. Two able bodied adults should be able to lift the TV on the wall, however a 3rd person supporting the weight in the middle may be needed. Also, plan your cables and power connectors before you mount everything up because you will not want to take this down later. Now on to the TV. It is absolutely stunning in terms of BRIGHTNESS. It advertises peak 3000 nits and honestly, it might hit it. I have a 77" QD-OLED TV and at 800-1000nits, this U7SG looks like the Sun compared to it. It is shockingly bright. No issues in full sunlight and in dark rooms and dark scenes, it will light up the room. The trade-off is blacks, while the full array local dimming and Hi-QLED MiniLED display, this display is still very good when it comes to black levels. Colors are absolutely stunning, you are going to have your jaw drop in any bright, animated or CGI moves. Motion is excellent, you also don't get the absolute pixel response times (this impacts how crisp images look in motion) as OLED, but 165Hz is fantastic and fast moving action movies and sports have no issues keeping up. Hockey, NASCAR, Soccer, all look amazing with no issues on this TV at all. I can't wait to see what the World Cup looks like on this TV. The green pitch will feel like you are in the game. I have a 5090 desktop, but I didn't get a chance to move it closer to my TV. Still, using the 5080 laptop showed what this display is capable of. I've been using Apple TVs for years to avoid the built-in OSes and because the processors in the TVs are generally much slower or get bogged down quickly by the increasing demands of bloated apps. Great feature! Google TV has some cool features and the tool tips show you how to use it, like holding the confirm button to go back to your last channel or app, holding up for stats in games etc. This TV also supports Dolby Vision and HDR10+ natively, which is great since my OLED did not support Dolby Vision which is super annoying. column8: review1 - ----- SUMMARY ----- Verdict: Taking down the old TV was quite the event in our house. As I was unmounting our couple-year-old QLED, my oldest just looked at me with genuine concern and asked, “What about Ms. Rachel?” I tried explaining the incredible mini-LED technology we were upgrading to, but toddler priorities are vastly different. However, the upgrade didn’t go unnoticed by the adults. I managed to get the Hisense 65” U7 Series fully mounted and dialed in while my wife was away. When she walked through the door and caught a glimpse of the screen, she literally did a double-take. “That must be the new TV,” she immediately noted. The difference really is that striking right out of the box. If you are coming from an older QLED or a standard LED panel, the jump to the Hisense U7 is massive. It solves the headache of bright-room viewing, packs in top-tier gaming features, and delivers a stunning picture. It offers a premium, flagship-level viewing experience at a price point that makes it an undeniable value, and I cannot recommend it enough. Pros: - Massive leap forward from older QLED or standard LED panels - Offers a premium, flagship-level viewing experience at an undeniable value - Excellent for bright-room viewing, virtually eliminating glare - Hi-QLED MiniLED Pro panel provides sheer brightness and uniform blacks - Top-tier gaming features including Native 165Hz and near-zero input lag - 2.1.2 Multi-Channel Sound tuned by Devialet delivers excellent, room-filling audio - Google TV interface is snappy and intuitive, eliminating the need for a separate streaming device - Included remote is premium and fully backlit Cons: - None ----- DETAILS ----- Design & Setup: Aesthetically, the 65-inch U7 Series looks incredibly sleek. It features a clean, unibody design with minimal bezels that allow the picture to stretch beautifully edge-to-edge. However, don’t let that thin profile fool you. This TV is deceivingly heavy. I initially thought I could handle getting it set up by myself, but with the weight distributed across 65 inches of screen, it’s quite difficult to manage alone. Whether you are wall-mounting it or just getting it situated on an entertainment center with the included stand, I definitely recommend grabbing a helper. Once it is finally in place, the sturdy build quality feels well-engineered and looks right at home in a modern living space. Display & Performance: This is where the U7 truly proves its worth. We have a lot of windows in our living room, and the bright Phoenix sun pouring in used to ruin daytime viewing unless we drew all the blinds. The anti-reflection, matte-like finish on this screen is an absolute game-changer. I can finally leave the windows open to enjoy the natural light without staring at my own reflection during dark cinematic scenes. Coupled with the glare reduction is the sheer brightness of the Hi-QLED MiniLED Pro panel. Powered by the Hi-View AI Engine Pro, it intelligently optimizes clarity and contrast in real time so nothing looks over-processed. The thousands of local dimming zones work remarkably well, pushing massive peak brightness right next to inky, uniform blacks without any distracting blooming, while the Pantone Validated colors keep every scene looking natural. Whether I’m throwing on an afternoon Diamondbacks game or watching a dark movie, the picture remains incredibly crisp, punchy, and fully visible regardless of the ambient light in the room. Audio Quality: I admittedly had low expectations for the built-in speakers. With my previous TVs, I almost immediately had to purchase a soundbar to get decent audio. However, I have been highly impressed by the sound quality of the U7. The 2.1.2 Multi-Channel Sound system is tuned by Devialet. I’m not well-versed in the audio world and had never heard of them before, but after doing some reading, I learned they are a highly regarded, high-end French acoustic engineering company. That pedigree definitely shows in this TV’s sound. It provides excellent, room-filling audio that can absolutely stand on its own or at least tide you over. While you are still going to get more punch out of a dedicated surround sound system, which this TV easily supports, the native audio is remarkably good. Gaming Capabilities: Between wrangling the kids and managing a generally busy lifestyle, I don’t get to game nearly as much as I used to. Because my free time is limited, finally getting the opportunity to sink into a visually demanding RPG like Cyberpunk 2077 on this TV is a real treat. I generally stick to single-player RPGs these days because I get way too frustrated trying to keep up in fast-paced shooters like Call of Duty like I did in my younger years. However, with the U7 Series being built for speed and clarity, I just had to give it a try to see how it handled. It features HDMI 2.1 inputs and supports a Native 165Hz refresh rate with AI Smooth Motion. Combined with Game Booster 330 and VRR, the motion clarity is exceptionally fluid, and the input lag is practically non-existent. It handled the chaos effortlessly, and I genuinely wish I had this TV back when my reflexes were actually competitive. It effectively doubles as a massive, high-performance gaming monitor. Smart Features, Interface & Remote: With almost every other TV I’ve owned, I always felt the immediate need to buy a dedicated streaming device because the native interface and built-in apps were so clunky and frustrating. I don’t feel that need at all with the U7. Running on Google TV with Gemini AI, the interface is incredibly snappy and intuitive, bringing personalized content discovery and voice control together in one seamless experience. Navigating between different streaming apps or quickly pulling up YouTube for the kids is completely frictionless. Enhancing that entire experience is the remote, which is genuinely the best I’ve ever used that came included with a TV. It looks premium, feels incredibly nice in the hand, and is fully backlit, a feature you rarely see but instantly appreciate when watching movies in the dark. Overall, the system doesn’t feel bogged down by bloated software. It just works smoothly and quickly. ----- WHAT’S IN THE BOX ----- 1 x Television 1 x Stand 1 x Power Cable 1 x Remote 1 x Quick Setup Guide 1 x User Manual ||| review2 - So, to be perfectly honest I was a bit hesitant to purchase another Hisense TV, the last one I had was a Android TV (which is what the TV’s operating system was called before it received a software update and became a Google TV). After the upgrade the TV did not function well, probably the fault of Google and not Hisense. Eventually I bought a Roku stick and got around that issue. So, once I saw the feature set of the 2026 model year of the U7 series I decided to give them another chance. The Hisense 65" U7 Series MiniLED QLED 4K HDR Smart TV has some interesting improvements including local LED dimming which aids in contrast and reduces “blooming” issues that are inherent in LED TVs, doesn’t quite match up with the inky blacks that my LG OLED TV produces, but good enough. So lets talk about the panel, it has an anti-reflective coating which does a good job reducing reflections. The remote control is backlit and automatically lights up when raised which is really cool, no fumbling with a button to enable backlighting. This TV is also pretty thin and has a easily installed stand that allows you to install the mount in two different positions, one to accommodate a soundbar. Speaking of sound, it has 2.1.2 Dolby Atmos sound and does a good job, although most TVs have less than Steller sound output from built in speakers. The display panel has a 165hz refresh rate, which is pretty good if you play video games (hooking up an xBox or PS5 via one of the four HDMI ports) One of the HDMI ports is of the eARC return audio variety which allows you to output sound to a A/V receiver. I have not yet done that to see it the digital signal will output a PCM Dolby Atmos data stream, something for me to test later if I decide to put this in my primary room where the Atmos capable A/V receiver and setup lives. Overall, I thought the display hit above its weight in image, the TV operating system was responsive (Google TV) and has many smart TV apps available, this TV also has Google’s Gemini AI built in so if you utilize Google’s ecosystem this maybe the right TV for you. Of course, the TV has Chromecast and Airplay 2, so no matter where you loyalties lie, this TV will work for casting. I won’t get too deep into the gaming controller compatibility since I did not test it, but supposedly you can you use a game controller with the TV. Two USB ports are provided, an optical output and an ethernet port for network connectivity, as well as Wi-Fi 6e compatibility, which is a nice feature, Wi-Fi 7 has not yet crept into smart TVs. Other options include sound output to a Bluetooth device such as speakers or headphones. This TV also includes an optical for basic digital output to a soundbar (will not pass advanced PCM streams though). The only issue I had was with the QR code-based setup which led me to an invalid link (Web parts not found), but that is something Hisense can fix on their website (or is that for Google to fix). Manual setup just required more typing and password input. Overall, if you are looking for a decent image and don’t want to spend a little more on an TV with an OLED based display, this “QLED TV” would be more than sufficient. Although since this is a 2026 model, you could potentially buy a previous year OLED for a similar price point as this 2026 model. >>> Pros >> decent contrast and blacks >> 3000 nits brightness, so this is a bright TV that can compensate for brightly lit rooms >> Backlit remote >>four HDMI ports >> Wi-Fi 6e >> ergonomic stand <<< Cons << not much, look for it on sale ||| review3 - For almost a decade now, OLED TVs and monitors have been the hot topic that everyone speaks highly of. Since then, there have been various iterations of OLED, LED, including quantum dot and mini LED variations. As a current QD-OLED & W-OLED monitor user and a former OLED TV user, this TV has rounded out my opinions on current display technologies, and honestly, I'm rather shocked by the results. FEATURE BREAKDOWN This TV uses Mini LEDs, plus quantum dot technology, with local dimming, matte anti-reflection, HDMI 2.1 bandwidth on all four inputs, 4K up to 165Hz, 1080p up to 330Hz, VRR, Dolby Vision, HDR10+, and DTS support. To be blunt, it has a brutally mean list of high end features at a mid-range price point. DISPLAY QUALITY The Hisense U7 MiniLED is made for all environments. Seriously. As someone who has used glossy reflective 4K panels for many years, this display breathes new life into my media library and living room setup. MiniLED is a massive win for folks who have bright sunbathed living room or bedroom entertainment setups. The 65 inch model of this display has 960 local dimming zones, which means that every small section of the display can be lit up independently. While there are displays with more local dimming zones and the ability to reach more than this TV's 3000 nits of peak brightness - this is the sweet spot. To elaborate more on that, in movie/TV scenes that have extremely bright or all white screens, the screen will get bright enough to make you squint - even if you're looking at your phone when the scene happens. This display simply gets that bright. I watched most of my content in the Standard preset with the brightness set to 50 out of 100, and if I went higher than that, the experience of an all-white screen was almost blinding. DISPLAY FEATURES Game mode reduces your input lag to almost nothing, which is great for any online gamers out there, and the motion clarity options provide the ability to clean up the usual stutter that can come from the cable TV shows which I tend to indulge in. While I am not a fan of motion clarity options on TVs historically, this TV does a fantastic job with judder reduction, which specifically has its own setting adjustment for maximum control. You can tweak the colors, motion, HDR capabilities, gamma, white balance, you name it. Control is key with any TV, and Hisense did a wonderful job of giving the ability to fully control your viewing experience. SOUND Folks, I recommend to everyone that they buy a TV for its display and not for the audio quality. While the audio quality on here is passable, it does not have bass or depth during complex audio sequences. I have no particular complaints about the audio quality, but you'll want a higher-end audio solution that matches that quality of the picture this TV provides. Since this TV has optical audio and eARC built-in, you have a wide array of audio options available to you. REMOTE Not my favorite remote, just to keep it simple. I don't have any issue with it, but I'd prefer something smaller and more ergonomic. While this is a smart TV with Android TV built in, you do have the option of hooking up an alternative smart TV platform with its own remote or simply pairing a different remote with this TV. FINAL THOUGHTS The Hisense U7 MiniLED QLED TV captures the features that most people care about. The dark inky blacks of OLED are not the end-all-be-all they once were. MiniLED QLED with local dimming gets us astonishingly close to OLED colors without the typical drawbacks of burn-in and low peak brightness. Couple that with a very handsome price point, and this TV becomes ideal for most consumers - myself included. Assembly Note: Be sure to follow the instructions carefully when attaching the base plate of the TV to the panel. It requires some balancing and you'll want someone helping you assemble and mount it. Open the box, read the instructions, then slowly follow them. ||| review4 - Hisense - 65" Class U7 Series MiniLED QLED UHD 4K HDR Smart Google TV (2026) Summary: A feature packed TV with a great display. Hisense is a brand that is evolving and clearly working hard on its climbing its way up by its competitive feature-packed offerings. Pros: * 4K beauty. It's been an issue for us across brands and technology and its noticeably less of an issue with this display. * TV OS/UI and Remote. The remote is svelte. As for longevity, we'll have to see as only time will tell. ||| review5 - Included- TV, stand, power cord, remote with batteries, user manual My first impression of the Hisense 65" Class U7 Series MiniLED QLED UHD 4K HDR Smart Google TV is that it's beautiful and great. Out of the box, the picture seemed pretty color accurate, which was surprising. I can probably dial it in a little better with a bit of time, but the colors appeared pretty close to accurate. The specs say it can do up to 3000 nits, and while I don't have equipment to verify that claim, I can say it is the brightest TV I have owned, and ambient light or indirect sunlight is not a problem. Viewing angles are a little disappointing, with a noticeable shift in brightness for those that are off center. So if you have a wide room, the best seats will be straight on. My only other trouble with the TV was not the TV's fault, but I have the unit connected into my Philips Hue Sync box and a Denon Receiver. When I connected my PC to the receiver, I could only get 120hz refresh rate. I later figured out this was a limitation of my receiver, and to get the faster 165Hz, I needed to plug my PC directly into the TV. At least there were 4 HDMI 2.1 ports that all work at 165Hz. Aside from that, the sound in the speakers are pretty good. They are not a good as having a soundbar or a Home Theater system, but they get the job done and are pretty good. Watching a movie and youtube video was great. column18: review1 - ----- SUMMARY ----- Verdict: Taking down the old TV was quite the event in our house. As I was unmounting our couple-year-old QLED, my oldest just looked at me with genuine concern and asked, “What about Ms. Rachel?” I tried explaining the incredible mini-LED technology we were upgrading to, but toddler priorities are vastly different. However, the upgrade didn’t go unnoticed by the adults. I managed to get the Hisense 65” U7 Series fully mounted and dialed in while my wife was away. When she walked through the door and caught a glimpse of the screen, she literally did a double-take. “That must be the new TV,” she immediately noted. The difference really is that striking right out of the box. If you are coming from an older QLED or a standard LED panel, the jump to the Hisense U7 is massive. It solves the headache of bright-room viewing, packs in top-tier gaming features, and delivers a stunning picture. It offers a premium, flagship-level viewing experience at a price point that makes it an undeniable value, and I cannot recommend it enough. Pros: - Massive leap forward from older QLED or standard LED panels - Offers a premium, flagship-level viewing experience at an undeniable value - Excellent for bright-room viewing, virtually eliminating glare - Hi-QLED MiniLED Pro panel provides sheer brightness and uniform blacks - Top-tier gaming features including Native 165Hz and near-zero input lag - 2.1.2 Multi-Channel Sound tuned by Devialet delivers excellent, room-filling audio - Google TV interface is snappy and intuitive, eliminating the need for a separate streaming device - Included remote is premium and fully backlit Cons: - None ----- DETAILS ----- Design & Setup: Aesthetically, the 65-inch U7 Series looks incredibly sleek. It features a clean, unibody design with minimal bezels that allow the picture to stretch beautifully edge-to-edge. However, don’t let that thin profile fool you. This TV is deceivingly heavy. I initially thought I could handle getting it set up by myself, but with the weight distributed across 65 inches of screen, it’s quite difficult to manage alone. Whether you are wall-mounting it or just getting it situated on an entertainment center with the included stand, I definitely recommend grabbing a helper. Once it is finally in place, the sturdy build quality feels well-engineered and looks right at home in a modern living space. Display & Performance: This is where the U7 truly proves its worth. We have a lot of windows in our living room, and the bright Phoenix sun pouring in used to ruin daytime viewing unless we drew all the blinds. The anti-reflection, matte-like finish on this screen is an absolute game-changer. I can finally leave the windows open to enjoy the natural light without staring at my own reflection during dark cinematic scenes. Coupled with the glare reduction is the sheer brightness of the Hi-QLED MiniLED Pro panel. Powered by the Hi-View AI Engine Pro, it intelligently optimizes clarity and contrast in real time so nothing looks over-processed. The thousands of local dimming zones work remarkably well, pushing massive peak brightness right next to inky, uniform blacks without any distracting blooming, while the Pantone Validated colors keep every scene looking natural. Whether I’m throwing on an afternoon Diamondbacks game or watching a dark movie, the picture remains incredibly crisp, punchy, and fully visible regardless of the ambient light in the room. Audio Quality: I admittedly had low expectations for the built-in speakers. With my previous TVs, I almost immediately had to purchase a soundbar to get decent audio. However, I have been highly impressed by the sound quality of the U7. The 2.1.2 Multi-Channel Sound system is tuned by Devialet. I’m not well-versed in the audio world and had never heard of them before, but after doing some reading, I learned they are a highly regarded, high-end French acoustic engineering company. That pedigree definitely shows in this TV’s sound. It provides excellent, room-filling audio that can absolutely stand on its own or at least tide you over. While you are still going to get more punch out of a dedicated surround sound system, which this TV easily supports, the native audio is remarkably good. Gaming Capabilities: Between wrangling the kids and managing a generally busy lifestyle, I don’t get to game nearly as much as I used to. Because my free time is limited, finally getting the opportunity to sink into a visually demanding RPG like Cyberpunk 2077 on this TV is a real treat. I generally stick to single-player RPGs these days because I get way too frustrated trying to keep up in fast-paced shooters like Call of Duty like I did in my younger years. However, with the U7 Series being built for speed and clarity, I just had to give it a try to see how it handled. It features HDMI 2.1 inputs and supports a Native 165Hz refresh rate with AI Smooth Motion. Combined with Game Booster 330 and VRR, the motion clarity is exceptionally fluid, and the input lag is practically non-existent. It handled the chaos effortlessly, and I genuinely wish I had this TV back when my reflexes were actually competitive. It effectively doubles as a massive, high-performance gaming monitor. Smart Features, Interface & Remote: With almost every other TV I’ve owned, I always felt the immediate need to buy a dedicated streaming device because the native interface and built-in apps were so clunky and frustrating. I don’t feel that need at all with the U7. Running on Google TV with Gemini AI, the interface is incredibly snappy and intuitive, bringing personalized content discovery and voice control together in one seamless experience. Navigating between different streaming apps or quickly pulling up YouTube for the kids is completely frictionless. Enhancing that entire experience is the remote, which is genuinely the best I’ve ever used that came included with a TV. It looks premium, feels incredibly nice in the hand, and is fully backlit, a feature you rarely see but instantly appreciate when watching movies in the dark. Overall, the system doesn’t feel bogged down by bloated software. It just works smoothly and quickly. ----- WHAT’S IN THE BOX ----- 1 x Television 1 x Stand 1 x Power Cable 1 x Remote 1 x Quick Setup Guide 1 x User Manual ||| review2 - So, to be perfectly honest I was a bit hesitant to purchase another Hisense TV, the last one I had was a Android TV (which is what the TV’s operating system was called before it received a software update and became a Google TV). After the upgrade the TV did not function well, probably the fault of Google and not Hisense. Eventually I bought a Roku stick and got around that issue. So, once I saw the feature set of the 2026 model year of the U7 series I decided to give them another chance. The Hisense 65" U7 Series MiniLED QLED 4K HDR Smart TV has some interesting improvements including local LED dimming which aids in contrast and reduces “blooming” issues that are inherent in LED TVs, doesn’t quite match up with the inky blacks that my LG OLED TV produces, but good enough. So lets talk about the panel, it has an anti-reflective coating which does a good job reducing reflections. The remote control is backlit and automatically lights up when raised which is really cool, no fumbling with a button to enable backlighting. This TV is also pretty thin and has a easily installed stand that allows you to install the mount in two different positions, one to accommodate a soundbar. Speaking of sound, it has 2.1.2 Dolby Atmos sound and does a good job, although most TVs have less than Steller sound output from built in speakers. The display panel has a 165hz refresh rate, which is pretty good if you play video games (hooking up an xBox or PS5 via one of the four HDMI ports) One of the HDMI ports is of the eARC return audio variety which allows you to output sound to a A/V receiver. I have not yet done that to see it the digital signal will output a PCM Dolby Atmos data stream, something for me to test later if I decide to put this in my primary room where the Atmos capable A/V receiver and setup lives. Overall, I thought the display hit above its weight in image, the TV operating system was responsive (Google TV) and has many smart TV apps available, this TV also has Google’s Gemini AI built in so if you utilize Google’s ecosystem this maybe the right TV for you. Of course, the TV has Chromecast and Airplay 2, so no matter where you loyalties lie, this TV will work for casting. I won’t get too deep into the gaming controller compatibility since I did not test it, but supposedly you can you use a game controller with the TV. Two USB ports are provided, an optical output and an ethernet port for network connectivity, as well as Wi-Fi 6e compatibility, which is a nice feature, Wi-Fi 7 has not yet crept into smart TVs. Other options include sound output to a Bluetooth device such as speakers or headphones. This TV also includes an optical for basic digital output to a soundbar (will not pass advanced PCM streams though). The only issue I had was with the QR code-based setup which led me to an invalid link (Web parts not found), but that is something Hisense can fix on their website (or is that for Google to fix). Manual setup just required more typing and password input. Overall, if you are looking for a decent image and don’t want to spend a little more on an TV with an OLED based display, this “QLED TV” would be more than sufficient. Although since this is a 2026 model, you could potentially buy a previous year OLED for a similar price point as this 2026 model. >>> Pros >> decent contrast and blacks >> 3000 nits brightness, so this is a bright TV that can compensate for brightly lit rooms >> Backlit remote >>four HDMI ports >> Wi-Fi 6e >> ergonomic stand <<< Cons << not much, look for it on sale ||| review3 - For almost a decade now, OLED TVs and monitors have been the hot topic that everyone speaks highly of. Since then, there have been various iterations of OLED, LED, including quantum dot and mini LED variations. As a current QD-OLED & W-OLED monitor user and a former OLED TV user, this TV has rounded out my opinions on current display technologies, and honestly, I'm rather shocked by the results. FEATURE BREAKDOWN This TV uses Mini LEDs, plus quantum dot technology, with local dimming, matte anti-reflection, HDMI 2.1 bandwidth on all four inputs, 4K up to 165Hz, 1080p up to 330Hz, VRR, Dolby Vision, HDR10+, and DTS support. To be blunt, it has a brutally mean list of high end features at a mid-range price point. DISPLAY QUALITY The Hisense U7 MiniLED is made for all environments. Seriously. As someone who has used glossy reflective 4K panels for many years, this display breathes new life into my media library and living room setup. MiniLED is a massive win for folks who have bright sunbathed living room or bedroom entertainment setups. The 65 inch model of this display has 960 local dimming zones, which means that every small section of the display can be lit up independently. While there are displays with more local dimming zones and the ability to reach more than this TV's 3000 nits of peak brightness - this is the sweet spot. To elaborate more on that, in movie/TV scenes that have extremely bright or all white screens, the screen will get bright enough to make you squint - even if you're looking at your phone when the scene happens. This display simply gets that bright. I watched most of my content in the Standard preset with the brightness set to 50 out of 100, and if I went higher than that, the experience of an all-white screen was almost blinding. DISPLAY FEATURES Game mode reduces your input lag to almost nothing, which is great for any online gamers out there, and the motion clarity options provide the ability to clean up the usual stutter that can come from the cable TV shows which I tend to indulge in. While I am not a fan of motion clarity options on TVs historically, this TV does a fantastic job with judder reduction, which specifically has its own setting adjustment for maximum control. You can tweak the colors, motion, HDR capabilities, gamma, white balance, you name it. Control is key with any TV, and Hisense did a wonderful job of giving the ability to fully control your viewing experience. SOUND Folks, I recommend to everyone that they buy a TV for its display and not for the audio quality. While the audio quality on here is passable, it does not have bass or depth during complex audio sequences. I have no particular complaints about the audio quality, but you'll want a higher-end audio solution that matches that quality of the picture this TV provides. Since this TV has optical audio and eARC built-in, you have a wide array of audio options available to you. REMOTE Not my favorite remote, just to keep it simple. I don't have any issue with it, but I'd prefer something smaller and more ergonomic. While this is a smart TV with Android TV built in, you do have the option of hooking up an alternative smart TV platform with its own remote or simply pairing a different remote with this TV. FINAL THOUGHTS The Hisense U7 MiniLED QLED TV captures the features that most people care about. The dark inky blacks of OLED are not the end-all-be-all they once were. MiniLED QLED with local dimming gets us astonishingly close to OLED colors without the typical drawbacks of burn-in and low peak brightness. Couple that with a very handsome price point, and this TV becomes ideal for most consumers - myself included. Assembly Note: Be sure to follow the instructions carefully when attaching the base plate of the TV to the panel. It requires some balancing and you'll want someone helping you assemble and mount it. Open the box, read the instructions, then slowly follow them. ||| review4 - Hisense - 65" Class U7 Series MiniLED QLED UHD 4K HDR Smart Google TV (2026) Summary: A feature packed TV with a great display. Hisense is a brand that is evolving and clearly working hard on its climbing its way up by its competitive feature-packed offerings. Pros: * 4K beauty. It's been an issue for us across brands and technology and its noticeably less of an issue with this display. * TV OS/UI and Remote. The remote is svelte. Thankfully, its not complicated stuff, but it would probably be better if it worked as intended. All in all, I'm impressed. I've always been an LG fan. We've had many of their LCDs and even their LCD projectors. This unit performs quite well and competes nicely with their mid-high tier options and especially so for their price point. As for longevity, we'll have to see as only time will tell. ||| review5 - Included- TV, stand, power cord, remote with batteries, user manual My first impression of the Hisense 65" Class U7 Series MiniLED QLED UHD 4K HDR Smart Google TV is that it's beautiful and great. column8: review1 - If you don't need 4k120hz (and you probably don't!) then this is a great tv for the money. Gaming on it is fantastic. I've already figured out the things I really like about it and there's a couple things that I don't which I will include in this review. For the price, the picture is absolutely excellent, way better than I expected. I bought this online so sight unseen based on other reviews that I read. It starts up fast when you hit the power button, and although I have not used Roku before, I'm pleased by some of the free options that I was able to download an ad very easily to the menu. I like that the menu is not crazy extensive and very easy to access to adjust brightness because I go from using this in lighter conditions, and then darker conditions so I can very quickly change that based on the environment. You can access more advanced display settings which can help fine tune the image that I already mentioned is very good, especially at this price point which I'm just stunned about. Also, the sound on this TV is very good, and the sound features are extremely good compared to any other TV I've owned. If I put this into speech mode, it actually reduces the background sounds better than any TV I've witnessed, from my own personal experience to my friends TVs which I've spent time watching. I guess I shouldn't be surprised because pioneer has been working in the sound industry for decades. Don't expect an extremely wide viewing angle without some loss of clarity because of the technology obviously, but that's true of all TVs that aren't OLED or wide parameter viewing monitors. I think the one thing I don't like is that if you're using an antenna, it doesn't allow you to manually add a particular channel, it just allows you to scan and access the channels It finds. This is particularly annoying because another TV in my house picks up some local channels that this does not find, and there is no way to add them manually, so please keep that in mind depending on your use. With all that being said, this is an extreme bargain and I think you get a lot more for your money buying pioneer, because some equally featured TVs are going to cost way more and I suspect it has to do with branding as pioneer has always been primarily an audio company. Absolutely pleased with this purchase.

I think the one thing I don't like is that if you're using an antenna, it doesn't allow you to manually add a particular channel, it just allows you to scan and access the channels It finds. This is particularly annoying because another TV in my house picks up some local channels that this does not find, and there is no way to add them manually, so please keep that in mind depending on your use. With all that being said, this is an extreme bargain and I think you get a lot more for your money buying pioneer, because some equally featured TVs are going to cost way more and I suspect it has to do with branding as pioneer has always been primarily an audio company. Absolutely pleased with this purchase.

column8: review1 - Our 5th Samsung TV over the last 15-20 years...we keep upgrading for size or technology. After six weeks with this one wall-mounted in a kitchen corner, it appears to be just as competent as the rest of them, which range up to a 75" Magnolia-level model. Good sound, good image, no hardware problems. Typical "issues" -- optimal viewing angle is about 45-60 degrees on either direction from head-on at 4' distance. Beyond that some slight degradation is noted in color balance and brightness, not in image quality overall. (Admittedly, we may be sitting too close to the set.) My other complaints apply to all my TV's: menu density is such that it takes, for example, nine or twelve button punches (depending on whether I start at Settings or at Home) on the remote to switch sound output from the device's speakers to Bluetooth. Bixby can alleviate that somewhat on the more upscale sets. It's also disturbing that Samsung doesn't allow for multi-source audio output; i.e., Bluetooth and device speakers simultaneously. Even on our bigger sets, where the option is provided, it never works as advertised when multiple viewers are trying to use different sound sourcepoints. What I'd really like is a way to set user defaults, so when I select myself as the viewer (as on our multi-viewer Netflix menu, for example) all my settings are automatically applied. All in all, we believe we got our money's worth. Got what we paid for? ||| review2 - I loved the color on my prior Toshiba which I had for 13 years, so you can imagine the difference from this 40" to my 37". I purchased Samsung because of it's reputation, but it's been a challenge to familarize myself to the changes, but I'm getting used to it. I was disappointed with the picture until I read some of the other reviews: "Optimal viewing angle is about 45-60 degrees on either direction from head-on at 4' distance. Beyond that some slight degradation is noted in color balance and brightness, not in image quality overall." Until I read this, I thought my TV might be broken. Although one channel has the washed out look even looking straight ahead. I wish the manual mentioned to expect this, I wouldn't have thought there was an issue. The sound is good. Also, the legs were wobbly, so I found a stand on Amazon. I had called Best Buy and I was really surprised they did not carry a pedestal stand or could refer me as to where to purchase one. The good thing is that there are features available to make picture adjustments, but who wants to be constantly making adjustments. I gave 3 stars for brightness because I thought it was too bright, but I was able to to decrease it and adjust the contrast. Still Samsung is still a first class company and you can always call them for assistance. ||| review3 - Quality TV for the price. column5: Hisense - 55" Class U6 Series MiniLED QLED UHD 4K HDR Smart Fire TV (2025)
column8: review1 - I am retired and build PCs and optimize TVs and stereo systems on the side. This TV was packaged normally. The legs are set so you can't put them on backwards. If you are coming from a Firestick, installation is simple. If not, you will have to download apps and enter passwords normally. It is built well, no flex at all. The TV is bright enough to show colors and great detail. It is not as bright as the next model up, but plenty bright. Picture quality is excellent, the blacks are surprising and on OLED level. Out of the box, calibration is very good, I saw no reason to change anything. There are five options on video and sound, surprisingly, there is a noticeable difference. I prefer filmmaker, sports and vivid, but that is subjective. If you don't care for presets, the menu has all the options to change to your taste. Processing is outstanding, much better that last years model. It upscales well enough that you may not see it necessary to wire directly. The new HDR 10+ is remarkable. I tested it wiring my PC to it having the most popular recent CPU and GPU, it performed well with low latency. No Game Bar, but I have found that it is not necessary if you have good input. Of course, use game mode. TVs have come a long way with sound. This one actually has a subwoofer and spatial sound. The new version of Dolby Atmos is impressive. With sound, same as video, 5 presets to choose from. I recommend you turn up the lowest 2 bands. 50 watts, plenty loud for a bedroom, small apartment, or small room. It is not the same as a quality soundbar or stereo output, It doesn't have booming bass, but I believe for most it will be acceptable. Think comparable to a new car stock stereo. Overall, if this is your budget, you will be pleased. Like anything else, you can always spend more for diminishing returns. One potential downfall: To meet the price point and picture quality given, it has a narrow field of view. This TV is designed to be sat in front of. If you have a large room, keep that in mind, but for a bedroom or small living room, no problem. For those who are unaware of the brand, Hisense is a manufacturer that has been making TVs since 1979, with nearly 19,000 employees. They are not as known in the US as worldwide. Their business model is different, building their own panels and parts, which costs less, and passing the savings along to consumers, and accepting less margins for mass production. Buy this, you will be happy. ||| review2 - I've been genuinely impressed with the 55 inch Hisense U65QF it truly punches above its weight class. What immediately caught my attention was the sheer brightness. The MiniLED and QLED combination makes HDR movies and shows just pop the colors feel incredibly vibrant, and the picture detail holds up even in a brightly lit room, which was a huge relief. Watching high-contrast scenes, the deep blacks are convincing, and the highlights are stunningly bright. As a casual gamer, the native 144Hz refresh rate has been a revelation. Games feel buttery smooth, and the responsiveness is virtually instant, which is a noticeable step up for fast-paced action. It's definitely a killer feature for the price point. Now for the couple of small drawbacks I've encountered. While the local dimming is very good overall, I sometimes catch a slight halo or "bloom" when a very bright logo or title card appears on a dark screen. It’s a minor annoyance. Also, the built-in Fire TV interface occasionally feels sluggish when I’m trying to jump quickly between apps, so I occasionally find myself waiting a beat too long. My final verdict? While the internal audio is just acceptable the picture quality is worth every penny. For anyone needing a bright, feature-packed 4K TV that excels at gaming without costing a fortune, I enthusiastically recommend this model. ||| review3 - This thin TV is so easy to set up. I only had to attach the two small stands that make up the base and plug it in. The two stands have a convenient "T" shape and two screws that make it impossible to install incorrectly. Once I turned it on, I was prompted to log in to my existing account, and all of my settings were imported. It recognized the Wi-Fi without me having to enter a password or search for a connection. I plugged in several other devices, and they were also quickly recognized and worked immediately. There are 4 HDMI inputs, so I was able to connect everything I wanted to. The picture is vibrant and sharp. I was impressed by the quality of the video and I was happy that I didn't have to spend any time adjusting colors to make everything look natural. It all looked great from the start! The only odd thing was that the enclosed manual was used for several different models. I suppose they all have the same easy set-up, but the instructions for this 55" model said it would take "at least three people" to set up due to the weight of the TV being 140 pounds! I knew from reading the description before I bought the TV that it only weighed about 30 pounds, so I knew that wasn't correct. It did give me a bit of a surprise, though, wondering how I was going to get that TV onto my existing TV stand! Of course, since that information was a bit inflated, the TV fit into the expected space perfectly. I'm very happy with the ease of set-up, the importation of all my information, and the built-in apps that make browsing easy and enjoyable. The manual could use some updating, though! ||| review4 - The Hisense 55" U6 Series really surprised me in a good way. For the price, the picture quality is honestly impressive. The screen gets plenty bright, which is perfect if you have a lot of windows or keep the lights on. Even during the day, the colors still pop and everything stays clear, so you’re not squinting to see what’s happening on screen. The Mini-LED and QLED combo gives movies and shows a nice, vibrant look without having to mess with a bunch of settings. Out of the box, it looks good enough that you can just turn it on and enjoy whatever you’re watching. Sports and fast scenes hold up well too, so it doesn’t feel blurry or laggy. What I like most is how easy it is to live with. Fire TV makes it simple to hop between apps, and the setup takes just a few minutes. Nothing complicated or frustrating. It feels like a TV that just fits into your routine without any drama. Overall, this model is a great pick if you want something bright, colorful, and modern without spending big money. It’s definitely a solid everyday TV that does a lot right and feels like a good value. ||| review5 - The 2025 Hisense 55U65QF miniLED with FireTV is an incredible value. It sits in the 'Entry-Level" price range, but has a host of specs and features you'd only expect in more-expensive models. 600 local dimming zones, and peak brightness of 1,000 nits allow for excellent contrast in dark to moderately-bright rooms. We have it on a stand in our small den, and it has done well coping with two adjacent windows to its side, and one window behind it. The setup was very simple. Given the option to use the remote or our phones, we chose to use our phone. The TV was connected via our Amazon account within minutes, and it allowed us to 'mirror' apps we had previously downloaded to another FireTV in our household. The FireTV interface is simple, clean and intuitive. We started enjoying our favorite streaming services immediately. 4K 60FPS videos streamed with no stutter, blockiness or signs of compression. While the room we placed it in is relatively small, the sound produced from the speakers is loud and clear. The controller is very small and easy to use. If I have one suggestion for improvement of this model, it would be making the remote feel a little bit more sturdy/premium in the hand. We were able to do some console gaming at 120FPS, and the TV handled it beautifully. This would be an excellent television for any modern gamer to enjoy. The FireTV can also be controlled via the app on your phone/mobile device, or from any Alexa device connected to your Amazon account. It's really cool to be able to say "Fire TV On" and have it turn on from across the room, or to mute the TV with your voice when a phone call comes in! There are just so many features to explore on the 55U65Q, that I'd run out of space if I tried. For a buyer that wants higher-end features at a lower-end price point, I'd make this TV a top contender for your next purchase. ||| review6 - I’m thoroughly impressed with the gameplay performance on this Hisense U6 Series MiniLED QLED TV. The variable refresh rate works flawlessly with both my Xbox Series X and PS5, delivering smooth, responsive action every time. The screen is bright and vibrant, easily lighting up the room, and it automatically adjusts to different lighting conditions — a big plus for any viewing environment. This TV truly feels like a steal for the price. My only minor drawback is that the Fire TV OS can occasionally feel a bit sluggish, even though there’s plenty of available memory. Overall, it’s an excellent buy with strong picture quality, gaming performance, and smart features. ||| review7 - Incredible value for what it delivers. The picture quality is shockingly good at this price point. The Mini-LED backlighting gives you deep contrast and bright highlights, while the QLED panel makes colors pop in a really natural way. Setup was easy, and since it’s a Fire TV, all my streaming apps were ready right away. Watching movies feels cinematic, and even casual gaming looks sharp with low input lag and Variable Refresh Rate support. But those are small trade-offs for what you get. If you’ve been thinking about upgrading your setup, this TV is proof that you don’t have to spend thousands for great performance. Highly recommend. ||| review8 - I’ve never owned a Hisense product before, but I have had a TV with Fire TV built in. That older TV is around eight years old now and always felt a bit slow, with certain apps crashing or freezing. I was nervous that upgrading might give me the same problems, but this Hisense U6 Mini-LED QLED UHR 4K TV has been a completely different experience. Setting it up straight out of the box was incredibly easy. I already had the Fire TV app on my phone, and it integrated with the new TV in ways I did not even know were possible with just 1 click. The whole thing took just a few minutes, and it felt completely seamless. We plan to mount the TV eventually, but even on the stand it felt sturdy and simple to handle. The padding and protective strip around the bezel made me feel more confident taking it out of the box. The first thing that impressed me was the picture quality. I could see such clear detail on faces in a show that is over ten years old. The colors are vibrant but not overly bright, and even though the TV gives you plenty of customization options, the default settings were already excellent. I usually tinker with picture settings on every TV and monitor I buy, but I did not need to this time. The speaker quality is good and has a fair range. I usually keep the volume low at night, but when we watch together as a family, we turn it up to around 20. It gets loud enough without any distortion, and we still had plenty of room to go higher. We did not use a soundbar. The TV speakers alone held up great. We use a lot of apps, and the responsiveness inside each app was solid. The only place I noticed a slight lag was on the main home page, but once you are in the app itself, everything runs smoothly. This model is 55 inches and fills our living room well, especially with the couch set a bit farther back. The TV also runs incredibly quietly. You do not hear anything coming from it. After watching for around 40 minutes to an hour, it did not feel warm to the touch. It stays cool, and whatever airflow system it uses works well without making noise. Overall, this TV has exceeded my expectations. The combination of Mini-LED, QLED, and 4K makes the picture stunning, the setup was effortless, and the everyday use has been enjoyable for both streaming and family watching. I can now confidently say that Hisense delivers quality in both style and performance, and I am genuinely happy with this purchase. ||| review9 - I began my review of the Hisense 55” Class U6 Series MiniLED QLED UHD 4K HDR Smart Fire TV (2025) with the unboxing process, which was remarkably straightforward. column8: review1 - For the size and price it is hard to justify complaining. Seeing as how the backlighting is consistent/bright across the screen with no bright spots (except for a light halo around the border with the screen black), the local dimming does not seem to be doing anything. However, the colors are richer. Images are not as sharp as I was expecting, but that could be due to the image being blown up/diluted so much. What is strange is how it struggles to sharpen normal images. Yet, it totally crushes digital images, like cartoons and graphics. Cartoons are extremely sharp and bright. Even on the same screen like the news, the people will be slightly blurry whole the graphics in the corner are very sharp and bright. The matte screen is not for me. The glare makes everything very washed out. One bright spot makes the whole screen sort of glow. This is definitely a dark room tv. Also, any angle of side viewing drastically reduces the quality. So, straight on viewing is important. The tv itself is very heavy. There are nice handles in the back to help you lift it. The base feet are pretty far apart. The remote is basic, but has nice tactile buttons. The google voice is a nice feature, but seems to be a bit slower than my other tv voice controls. The built-in handles on the back made a huge difference—I’m only 4’11 and he’s 5’9, so lifting it was definitely a challenge, but manageable. I was surprised by how much metal there is on the back and how heavy it is. At 124 lbs, it’s heavier than our 100-lb-rated stand, so we’ll be reinforcing it to make sure there are no issues. Once we had the legs on, setup and registration were quick and easy. Even though our new TV stand hasn’t arrived yet, we couldn’t resist trying it out. The difference in color and crispness is amazing, and the size is perfect for our living room. We usually watch TV while eating dinner, and this will make that even more enjoyable, especially when family visits. I love the screensaver option with personal photos, and I plan to update it with recent family pictures soon. The remote is also super convenient—having quick buttons for Netflix, Disney+, and other apps saves time compared to navigating menus. Overall, we’re thrilled with this upgrade—it’s already making our movie nights and everyday viewing so much better! ||| review3 - I was hesitant on buying a Hisense TV since I knew nothing about the brand. When mounted the stand is very sturdy, I was worried it would be flimsy and scared to let my son near it, but it holds up amazing. When you turn the TV on it has to be setup, it takes about 15 min and is very easy. You can connect your Google account. A really cool feature is you can out your personal photos as a screen saver! Im very impressed with the quality of the picture and the responsiveness. It's so clear you would think the people were real! ||| review4 - The Hisense - 98" Class QD5 Series QLED 4K UHD Smart Google TV checks all the boxes with my family and I. It’s a great addition to our media room and my kids are in love with the larger than life picture. The picture quality is outstanding and movie watching experience is great. Sports our spot on as the refresh rate is fantastic. Sound quality is perfect in our space, no need for external speakers. User interface is excellent and very user friendly, even for children. Remote could me better quality in my opinion, but still good. Overall we couldn’t be happier. ||| review5 - We recently bought a 98-inch Hisense TV and it’s honestly amazing. The screen is huge and feels like having a mini movie theater at home. The picture quality is very clear and bright, especially when watching movies or sports. The sound is also good even without extra speakers. The setup was pretty easy, but because it’s very big, you definitely need help moving or installing it. For the price, it’s a great deal compared to other brands with the same size. Overall, we’re very happy with this TV. If you want a big screen for your living room, the 98-inch Hisense TV is definitely worth it. Another plus point, It connects to Amazon Alexa, so you can easily turn the TV on or off when you’re sleepy or far from the remote. ||| review6 - I’m extremely happy with this TV and feel it offers great value for the price. The design is sleek and modern, with thin bezels that give it a premium look. It fits perfectly in my living room and feels well-built. Overall, this TV delivers excellent performance, user-friendly features, and solid build quality. At 98 inches, it feels like having a full-on movie theater at home. I had been considering getting a projector for that big-screen experience, but I’m so glad I went with this TV instead. Overall, I’m really happy with this TV. ||| review8 - The Photos I posted don't do this TV Justice. This tv is amazing, not only in its size but in its price as well. My first thought was this needs to be placed across the other side of a room. Totally not the case. I have this tv 8 to 10' from my sitting area depending on what side of the couch you sit on. Its not too big. The picture quality is amazing. Its so much more realistic. The dark scenes aren't so dark. The sound quality from the built in speakers is great as well it adapts to the area your in. It doesn't get soft and loud when changing from a movie to a commercial The built in Google software and available videos are so smooth and transitioning from one to another is simple and easy. If you're looking for a new tv. Take a look at this one. Make a step up and get the size. You won't regret it. Everyone I have shown this tv to loves it. ||| review9 - This TV is massive (98 inch) and super high quality! Even though it’s large the coloring and uniformity of the screen are very high quality. The tv picture looks pretty great. My only issue is we are big YouTube TV people which Google TV is supposed to have. However when we try to find the app or search it says item not found (see attatched photo) so that’s been pretty annoying. Having to chromecast from my phone until we figure it out. This TV is great for watching sports and also very cinematic for movies! It’s perfect for an mancave or home theatre! Overall would highly recommended this TV for the man cave! ||| review10 - Love this TV. Shows an incredible picture. It was bought to replace a projector and theater screen. I might be concerned if mounting on wall without support. ||| review11 - I like Everything about this television, size is just right, I can maje the picture fo what I want!! The price wasn't bad either,,If I had a bigger house I would buy another just like it! ||| review12 - This TV is a multimedia giant. The Android OS interface is smooth, fast, and super responsive. I created TV profiles that make parental controls a breeze! The remote has a premium feel though it’s a bit larger than it needs to be. The TV frame itself doesn’t feel cheap at all, and the built-in handles make installation a breeze for two people, even with its size and weight. Image quality? Absolutely stunning. Bright scenes, sports, and cartoons all look incredibly vibrant colors pop without looking over-processed or artificial. I was using a 4K projector in this space, and even at max brightness and color settings, it doesn’t come close to the Hisense 98” QD5. The difference is so dramatic, I’ve already packed up the projector. This TV is now the centerpiece in our loft. A few out-of-the-box tweaks are necessary: There’s noticeable blooming in dark scenes when there are small bright elements on screen. Thankfully, this can be mostly fixed with a few setting adjustments that significantly reduce the issue. Sound-wise, the auto mode is fine for casual TV, but the soundstage feels narrow for movies. Switching to Theater mode brings the audio to life. Boost the subwoofer level a bit and it's honestly enjoyable without a soundbar. That said, a soundbar definitely enhances the experience though I do wish the TV's built-in speakers could work in tandem with external audio gear. ||| review13 - I am so impressed by this TV! This Hisense TV supports Apple AirPlay for smooth streaming and also integrates with Apple Homekit and works with Alexa for smart control. I like how it features 4 ports of HDMI 2.1 so I can plug in other devices. The screen has such rich, vibrant, and realistic color. The 98” screen size creates a truly cinematic experience at home. My husband wanted a projector, but we realized that the quality wouldn't compare against a TV. This was a great purchase that exceeded expectations and all my friends and family are jealous when they see it. Overall, Hisense made an amazing TV with a huge screen and pleasurable viewing experience. ||| review18 - We upgraded from a 2020 Hisense 75" Android TV to the 98" QD5 QLED, and after a week, we're really impressed. Motion can be slightly uneven in fast scenes, but overall, this is a fantastic upgrade for a cinematic home setup. ||| review19 - PLEASE NOTE: the 3 stars is for misleading size specifications, not picture quality, which I cannot even test at this point. The ONLY reason I bought this TV was because it said in multiple places the legs are 50" apart, which would fit my existing 55" stand. Though there is 1 image that says 59.9" apart, a review of the Q&A at the time (black friday) showed 50" to be accurate. For $999 at the time, I bought it and scheduled a closer to Xmas delivery to surprise the mister, who'd wanted at least a 75" upgrade. I figured this was a "hold my beer" moment to REALLY surprise him. Yeah, well, BOTH of these measurements are wrong - the inside distance is 69" apart as we found out only after clearing off the old TV, maneuvering this beast into our room, and then tearing off the protective bag to install the legs. Yeah, no. Not even close to 50" or even 59.9" as shown on the website, and of course now there's a review from 25 days ago that says the legs are 69" apart. Now I'm faced with either returning it or spending another chunk of $$$ to get a different stand, which is ALSO a problem as so far the only TV console wide enough to accommodate the 19" legs is $599. So yeah... BUYER BE AWARE... and no, I don't mean "beware" because I'm sure it's a great TV otherwise. I wouldn't know because I haven't got a place to use it yet thanks to this kerfuffle. If we keep it I'll update later with a quality review, but for now I'm too frustrated at the ruined gift to make a decision. So to recap - THE STAND LEGS ARE ~69" APART (~70" outer width) and *NOT* the 50" as advertised. ||| review20 - This TV is more than I expected. column8: review1 - Did a long overdue upgrade on my main tv. The color range and anti glare have been a really nice change with the window in the room normally making the old tv unviewable, now minimally impacted. This is my second oled, first one from samsung. There are a few features I miss like the option for art screen savers like lg offers, while samsung does have its own screen savers none have the same character that the lifelike art lg provides really showcasing the oled. The free channels have been a really nice perk to the samsung as I dont pay for cable, but having the option for local news through the tv with minimal ads has been nice. The ui for the apps and some menus does leave things to be desired, the remotes minimalist design does force you to navigate the menus slightly more. (I switch inputs a decent amount and it requires you to goto the menu and flip through the tabs. I like lg having it as a button standard on the remote.) I currently have a LG C4, a Sony X85J, and now this samsung S90F. The tv is a little harder to set up with a PC than the lg in terms of ui and it occasionally resetting when nothing changed but the high refreshrate being there was really needed with the old tv maxing out at 30hz. The sound is overall okay on its own, but when you step into this price range, I'd assume you are either already planning on a soundbar or speakers. Tl;dr the color is great, the anti glare fixes about 80-90% of really bad glare from a large window. The features are great. Would still recommend a soundbar or speakers. Only miss small niche things. ||| review2 - The brightness, clarity, colors, and blacks on this thing are insane. I didn't think I was missing that much not switching to oled yet but even all of my favorite older movies feel like I'm watching an entirely new or remastered movie. I havent played any games yet but I'm sure it will be epic. ||| review3 - Excellent television. Picture quality is incredible. Colors are vibrant, and of course, blacks are true blacks in this OLED.
