column8: review1 - Absolutely impressed with this TV. The picture quality is incredibly sharp and clear, with vibrant colors and true 4K detail. The sound quality is also surprisingly good — rich, clean, and immersive without needing extra speakers. The overall design feels very premium and modern, making it look high-end in the living room. Great value for the price and definitely exceeded my expectations. ||| review2 - I had never considered buying a Hisense TV before, it was a brand I didn’t know much about, and I was very wary about whether it would be up to my “standards”. After having the Hisense 75” U7 MiniLED Google TV for a few days I can humbly acknowledge that this TV exceeds my expectations with ease. My only complaint is about the weight and how bulky it feels, and it was because of these two that I was initially inclined to give it a 4-star rating, but I think it is closer to a 5-star rating. The main selling point for this device is the picture/video capabilities, which I think are outstanding. Even older content looks decent (which is not always the case for TVs of this big size), I assume there is some sort of correction or upscaling that comes into play, and I think Hisense has done a great job in that regard. For newer content I perceived some image adjustment a few times (I have yet to determine the conditions but looks like there is always some sort of adjustment/processing to the image). Nevertheless, the end result feels just great. I paired this the Hisense U7 TV with my existing 360 audio setup, connected to the TV through e-ARC HDMI, and we have been enjoying watching videos on YouTube and Netflix, which are the two major apps we use to consume content, besides regular cable TV. • Pros: bright and vivid colors, no glare, no reflection, high refresh rate. • Cons: very heavy. little bulky, only 2.1 audio. >> Assembly It is recommended to have two people unpack and assembly it. I took the risk and assembled it on my own on the carpet; however, I had to resort to my significant other to place the TV on the media console furniture, as it was impossible for me to do it alone. The base stand is very heavy, which is expected if you don’t want to risk the TV tilt over. If you are thinking about putting this TV on the wall, I’d think twice, it is very heavy and I am sure you’d need to have a solid TV wall mount and wall or studs that can hold the mount plus the TV without incurring much stress. For now, I am keeping the TV on a media console table until I find a replacement for my older entertainment center furniture which only fits up to my older 65” TV. >> Setup Just follow the on-screen instructions. It forces you to login to your google account or create on if you don’t have it, it is a Google TV after all. For privacy reasons I always like to have this kind of devices to not contain any of my personal information, so I reluctantly added my seldom used Google account. You could argue that I could have just created a Google account for the TV and forget about it (next time). Besides this initial Google account observation, the rest of the setup is very easy. >> Picture/Video The picture quality of this device is outstanding. The default settings provide a very bright image, which could strain your eyes at night, so you’d need to perform some image adjustments (change for instance to night theater mode). In the image settings section, there is the AI “intelligent settings” to allow personalize the image, we haven’t tried it as we find the current options are all that we need, but that is something you might want to explore. Content in 4K and higher looks amazing. Also, lower quality videos look decent enough to watch them without much complaint, which is not always true for similar size TVs, so there must be some sort of image adjustment. For newer content there also seems to be some image processing, since a few times I noticed the images/videos to look “retouched” (similar to what you get with AI-generated content). I guess is the work of the miniLED technology. Add to this a high refresh rate of 165Hz and I can enjoy videos and play games without noticing any choppiness. I believe Hisense has a solid product right here. >> Audio This comes with only 2.1.2 multichannel configuration, which I haven’t tested since I went straight to connect the TV with my 360 audio equipment through e-ARC HDMI, and the sound is just perfect. I was curious why it didn’t come with more channels though, and it looks like there is another version of this TV, the U8 series, which has more channels, and that might be something to consider before buying either model. >> Apps There are multiple apps available for this TV, as expected. I was surprised that the Hisense app has a good set of free channels, similar to the older 65” TV I am replacing this TV with (well, I’ll still keep the older TV though). And in the age of AI, it is no surprise that we encounter AI apps everywhere, and this TV is no exception. The main AI app one of course is Gemini, but there is another simple one that caught my eye, the “custom AI art” app. Custom AI art: I tried this app just for curiosity and was highly pleased with it, it looks simple on the surface but for sure produces amazing looking images. I can create a screen saver with these AI generated images, but the only downside to use them as screen saver is that it forces you to link your account to the TV, which I think is a little intrusive. ||| review3 - I upgraded TVs, going from a 55” budget TV to this 75” Hisense TV. While the difference in size was huge, the difference in quality was even more significant. My old TV was a little less than a decade old, and I wanted something larger where I could both enjoy my media and play on my PS5. I have been using this TV for about a week now, and wow, what a breathtaking upgrade this is. In this review, I will go over my thoughts on the Hisense – 75” Class U7 Series 4K Google TV. *TLDR at the bottom =================================== IN THE BOX/SET-UP: The TV was packed and shipped nicely. Kudos to the logistics team! In the box, you get a heavy television stand, power cable, backlit remote, and some documentation. You will need two people to set the TV up due to its awkward and large size. I recommend double-checking inside the Styrofoam inserts, as there were a couple of items in there that I would’ve thrown away if I hadn’t found them at the last minute. The instructions were straightforward, and you should expect to spend at least 30 minutes setting the TV up. My entertainment center has a built-in mount, so I had to do some cleanup, and therefore, my setup time was a bit over an hour. If you plan to mount the TV, there are screws in the back that need to be removed in order to attach a mount there. Once the physical setup was complete, I needed to go through the TV setup. The TV runs Google TV, which is based on Android. The UI is very Android-heavy and will be familiar to Android users. A Google account is required for setup. =================================== FIRST IMPRESSIONS: My first impression of this TV is wow, it’s massive. Going from a 55” to a 75” is a huge difference and feels significantly more immersive. There are also plenty of HDMI ports for all your devices(4 HDMI ports, 1 is HDMI eARC). One major item that will stand out upon turning up the volume is the TV's speakers. They are tuned by Devialet and sound amazing. They are probably the best built-in TV speakers I have ever heard. The built-in subwoofer adds what most TVs lack, which is the lows. There is also an EQ setting available to fine-tune the audio to your liking. Now, can these built-in speakers replace a home theatre audio system? No, you won’t be receiving that surround and immersive sound with the built-in speakers. But if you don’t have anything else, the TV's speakers are perfect and work well. They seriously do sound great. On top of sounding great, Hisense offers the ability to run both the TV's speakers and your optical connected speakers at the same time for an even grander experience. The remote being backlit is also a nice touch. =================================== PICTURE QUALITY: In terms of picture quality, as soon as you start something up on the TV, you will be immersed in vivid imagery. One of the first things I did was watch one of those 4K scenic videos with vibrant colors on YouTube. There are plenty of TV modes ranging from Vivid to theatre modes. I decided to test out the brightness first, and this TV does get bright indeed. It gets up to 3000 nits peak brightness. In a fully lit room, the display continues to look amazing! On top of that, the mini-LED QLED display allows you to view the display from any angle without the picture getting “washed out.” One of my favorite parts of this TV is the color detail. All colors are distinguishable from each other and appear incredibly vibrant and realistic. Watching true 4K content on this TV is seriously an eye-catching experience. Darker scenes on your media where there are different shades of black are also distinguishable with little to no blooming. Do you prefer watching media in a different tone? The picture settings (blacks, white balance, contrast, gamma, etc.) are quite vast on this TV, and you can genuinely spend a good amount of time messing with the settings. =================================== FEATURES/PERFORMANCE: The TV is powered by Google TV. The UI is easy to navigate and straightforward. Apps can also be downloaded via the custom Play Store, which includes Google Play Games. I didn’t get a chance to play around with Google Play Games, but the free games are a nice touch. The remote is also voice-enabled and can be used to search for things rather than manually typing words out. As with most smart devices these days, there are “AI-powered” features on this TV. Google’s Gemini is built into here as an assistant. I haven’t played around with Gemini, but according to Google, it should be able to personalize recommendations based on the stuff you ask. The AI stuff I played around with more is the TV’s AI features. Some of these include AI Contrast, which automatically adjusts dark and light areas based on the scene. Which seemed to work subtly, but not anything significant. Another AI feature that I was interested in but left me a bit dissatisfied is the AI Ambient Light Sensor. This feature is supposed to automatically adjust brightness based on the room’s lighting, but I found that it would adjust brightness a little too much on one side. For example, in a dark room, the brightness would be turned down way too low to the point where the picture loses its clarity. In terms of performance, the TV does an excellent job of playing your favorite media in stunning quality. Picture quality can be adjusted to your liking, so whether you like that cool or warm look, there are plenty of customization options for you. The TV can also be used for gaming. With a 4K display and up to a native 165Hz refresh rate, console gaming is perfect for this TV. While the PS5 can only do up to a 120Hz refresh rate, it was still able to take advantage of the various picture settings. One neat feature that I found was that the PS5’s main menu can be controlled with the TV remote. Anything beyond that, you’ll need your gaming controller. Within the TV’s menu, there is a Game Bar-like option that pulls up various game settings. Some of these settings include changing game modes (e.g., FPS, RPG, etc.). There is an option to turn on an FPS counter and a setting to enhance dark details, which is great for those horror games that are too dark. I was able to play a variety of games, from racing to action-adventure games like Gran Turismo and Kena: Bridge of Spirits. Overall, both looked incredible. I did turn on Fidelity mode in games that supported it to maximize picture quality. With this turned on, combined with the fine details that the TV brings out in games, everything was certainly breathtaking. Overall, if you enjoy console gaming on large TVs, this is a perfect TV for your console. If you want to simply use the TV for your favorite TV shows/films, this TV will give you everything you need for an immersive experience. =================================== CONCLUSION/TLDR: Overall, this Hisense TV has been a fantastic upgrade from my previous one. I seriously enjoy how detailed and vivid the picture quality is. From the brightest of colors to the various shades of black, this TV enhances it all to make it feel more immersive. The picture settings are highly customizable. Whether you like the darker details to be brighter or if you would rather watch your film in a cooler color, it's all open to customization. The speakers on this TV are one of the highlights as they sound incredible. The built-in subwoofer brings out the lows that many TVs lack. On top of being able to view your favorite media in stunning quality, the TV can also be used for gaming. I used my PS5 with this TV, and my entire gaming experience became more immersive. My old TV was close to a decade old, and I didn’t realize how many new features I was missing out in modern TVs. This TV can do it all, and if you are looking for an upgrade, I wholeheartedly recommend you try this one out! ||| review4 - Getting the TV ready is the same as any TV. The one thing I did have a problem with though is that the app clip on iOS didn't work. When you turn it on, it says scan the QR code to easily be able to setup the TV, and all I got was an error on my iPhone so I couldn't use it. I had to go in manually using the controller, and since you're forced to sign into google account and I have a long password, it was a long process. The only other annoyance is all the apps that come pre installed and having to remove them. But since the TV runs google TV (aka Android TV) if you have google play store apps they can be loaded and I believe would save your home screen if you have another device. With the bad out of the way, the rest of my experience has been great. The smart TV software isn't actually too bad and I have been using it after installing another launch. Usually I switch to a connected HDMI device but this has been snappy and works pretty decent so I use it more then any other TV. Beyond the software, the picture is the big thing and you'll notice it if you're going from a super cheat TV to this. The blacks look amazingly black, and the colors are all amazing. If you do use OLED this is the closet I've seen to color like this that's not OLED. The refresh rate is also impressive if you're playing games or watching sports. The speaker are all decent, though I did go back to using my sound bar for surround sound but if you don't have that setup the included speakers do sound good. Other features are pretty similar, you get 4 hdmi port though weirdly ARC is 3 and not 1 so plug it correctly. The controller is responsive but nothing special and also has the random buttons for apps to stream with. Overall, this is a really nice TV with a working smart system that responds and one you'll use. The picture is superb and rivals OLED with a fast refresh rate. ||| review5 - I decided to step up from a 65" to a 75" TV. I am glad I ended up with this TV. First, I do not have a wall mount. I have been using a coffee table. My old TV had legs at each end. This on the other hand, has a mount in the middle. So, plenty of room. You can choose to mount it with the stand in 2 positions. One slightly higher if you prefer it to be a bit higher. This was just perfect for my sound bar to sit in front and not be too tall. I am impressed with this TV and so is my family. Our old TV was Samsung. Was great when we got it, but always just felt a bit dark. Shows that had dark scenes where hard to see. Same with gaming on it. Watching sports and non-dark shows, games and movies was fine. But just that, fine. Got this and right away we noticed it was a lot clearer and brighter. First thing wife wanted to do was find this episode of a show she was watching to see how it looked because it had a dark scene and this TV did not disappoint for that scene. We were able to see what was happening. Gaming just feels smooth and feels instant. Games also just have a much better vibrant color to them and just have an overall fun experience. 4k with 120 to 165hz looks amazing. I was using an Xbox to game with, and I just can't get over how this TV looked. Shooter games were a lot easier to see someone in corners and in dark areas. My oldest son has a PS5 and kept wanting to kick me off to plug in his PS5. Sports were a blast to watch as well. Right now, mainly baseball and basketball. I look forward to watching fights, as well as football. Just an overall crystal-clear experience. The remote. Love how it looks and love that it lights up when you lift it. But you can also set up your phone and use your phone. So that was a huge plus. At the moment, I am just in aw with watching movies, shows and playing games. I will say one negative thing for me. That is that the USB ports seem too not get power if the TV is turned off. I highly recommend this TV, especially if you are a gamer or enjoy sports or even TV shows or movies. This makes them clear and vibrant.

But if you don’t have anything else, the TV's speakers are perfect and work well. They seriously do sound great. On top of sounding great, Hisense offers the ability to run both the TV's speakers and your optical connected speakers at the same time for an even grander experience. The remote being backlit is also a nice touch. =================================== PICTURE QUALITY: In terms of picture quality, as soon as you start something up on the TV, you will be immersed in vivid imagery. One of the first things I did was watch one of those 4K scenic videos with vibrant colors on YouTube. There are plenty of TV modes ranging from Vivid to theatre modes. I decided to test out the brightness first, and this TV does get bright indeed. It gets up to 3000 nits peak brightness. In a fully lit room, the display continues to look amazing! On top of that, the mini-LED QLED display allows you to view the display from any angle without the picture getting “washed out.” One of my favorite parts of this TV is the color detail. All colors are distinguishable from each other and appear incredibly vibrant and realistic. Watching true 4K content on this TV is seriously an eye-catching experience. Darker scenes on your media where there are different shades of black are also distinguishable with little to no blooming. Do you prefer watching media in a different tone? The picture settings (blacks, white balance, contrast, gamma, etc.) are quite vast on this TV, and you can genuinely spend a good amount of time messing with the settings. =================================== FEATURES/PERFORMANCE: The TV is powered by Google TV. The UI is easy to navigate and straightforward. Apps can also be downloaded via the custom Play Store, which includes Google Play Games. I didn’t get a chance to play around with Google Play Games, but the free games are a nice touch. The remote is also voice-enabled and can be used to search for things rather than manually typing words out. As with most smart devices these days, there are “AI-powered” features on this TV. Google’s Gemini is built into here as an assistant. I haven’t played around with Gemini, but according to Google, it should be able to personalize recommendations based on the stuff you ask. The AI stuff I played around with more is the TV’s AI features. Some of these include AI Contrast, which automatically adjusts dark and light areas based on the scene. Which seemed to work subtly, but not anything significant. Another AI feature that I was interested in but left me a bit dissatisfied is the AI Ambient Light Sensor. This feature is supposed to automatically adjust brightness based on the room’s lighting, but I found that it would adjust brightness a little too much on one side. For example, in a dark room, the brightness would be turned down way too low to the point where the picture loses its clarity. In terms of performance, the TV does an excellent job of playing your favorite media in stunning quality. Picture quality can be adjusted to your liking, so whether you like that cool or warm look, there are plenty of customization options for you. The TV can also be used for gaming. With a 4K display and up to a native 165Hz refresh rate, console gaming is perfect for this TV. While the PS5 can only do up to a 120Hz refresh rate, it was still able to take advantage of the various picture settings. One neat feature that I found was that the PS5’s main menu can be controlled with the TV remote. Anything beyond that, you’ll need your gaming controller. Within the TV’s menu, there is a Game Bar-like option that pulls up various game settings. Some of these settings include changing game modes (e.g., FPS, RPG, etc.). There is an option to turn on an FPS counter and a setting to enhance dark details, which is great for those horror games that are too dark. I was able to play a variety of games, from racing to action-adventure games like Gran Turismo and Kena: Bridge of Spirits. Overall, both looked incredible. I did turn on Fidelity mode in games that supported it to maximize picture quality. With this turned on, combined with the fine details that the TV brings out in games, everything was certainly breathtaking. Overall, if you enjoy console gaming on large TVs, this is a perfect TV for your console. If you want to simply use the TV for your favorite TV shows/films, this TV will give you everything you need for an immersive experience. =================================== CONCLUSION/TLDR: Overall, this Hisense TV has been a fantastic upgrade from my previous one. I seriously enjoy how detailed and vivid the picture quality is. From the brightest of colors to the various shades of black, this TV enhances it all to make it feel more immersive. The picture settings are highly customizable. Whether you like the darker details to be brighter or if you would rather watch your film in a cooler color, it's all open to customization. The speakers on this TV are one of the highlights as they sound incredible. The built-in subwoofer brings out the lows that many TVs lack. On top of being able to view your favorite media in stunning quality, the TV can also be used for gaming. I used my PS5 with this TV, and my entire gaming experience became more immersive. My old TV was close to a decade old, and I didn’t realize how many new features I was missing out in modern TVs. This TV can do it all, and if you are looking for an upgrade, I wholeheartedly recommend you try this one out! ||| review4 - Getting the TV ready is the same as any TV. column8: review1 - I own 3 TCL TVs bought 5 years apart. This is my 4th. All work flawlessly. I got this 50" TCL QM5K TV on sale for a great price. It appears to be a Best Buy exclusive. I use this as a computer monitor and a TV in my office. With a little tweaking it has crystal clear text and images as a monitor. I tried using a TCL 4 series as a monitor. Excellent budget TV but as a monitor -NOPE, ghosted text and just not precise enough. This TV is a work horse. Great gaming monitor but you are limited to 60fps because of the refresh rate. The compromises over the larger QM series are fewer dimming zones, a slightly less powerful image processor and a 60hz panel. I think because of this standard definition processing is a little 'blotchy' but imminently watchable, depending on the source but with higher resolution in HD and UHD the picture is what you'd want from a QLED TV. Blac levels are black. No blooming. See the dandelion photo. It has a very low glare screen. Minimal reflections. Picture is bright even in a sunlit room. The sound is actually quite good for a TV. No bass of course. The images I included are very close to the actual display. Yours may vary. Additionally, I'm a ROKU fan but the built in Google interface is admittedly very good; very snappy. I had an extra ROKU stick that has all my logons and preferences already installed or I would use the the Google interface. I also hope all Best Buy staff are as responsive as this store. I wanted this TV but was sold out at the time. I went back a couple days later and they had two just come in still in plastic wrap buried in a 'Jenga' looking palette. The sales person politely said, "I can't sell you those yet". I asked to speak to a manager and explained I am here to buy this TV not just look. At first he also said couldn't do it - not yet in inventory. I explained but if I wait they could be sold when I come back later. He said hang on a minute and left to check if they were reserved for online orders. They were not. Rather than pass up the sale the manager deviated a bit from their usual process and carefully removed the TV from the stack, logged it into inventory on the spot and said get your vehicle and we'll have it for you out front. Outstanding customer service! I knew they could have stuck with their rules but instead they made the sale. Thank you to that manager and thanks to Best Buy. Also, this isn't the first time staff at my local Best Buy have worked with me to do what they could to make a sale I was happy with or offer an unsolicited suggestion that saved me money and lowered their profit but increased my loyalty. I'll always check with Besy Buy before looking online. They are often higher on little things but usually match online prices with big ticket items. And easy returns. That instant response to the customer is lost if we lose our 'brick and mortar' stores. ||| review2 - I bought this TV during the 2025 Holiday/EoY sale for about 50% off, and have had a chance to put it through its paces. A point on AI features: The motion smoothing can be a little artifacty around certain objects at times when turned up to a high setting when combined with the dynamic contrast in intelligent mode. Maybe a software update can fix this later, just be aware that this does happen occasionally if you are a heavy motion smoothing user. What you get: Great quality picture for the price. Dolby Vision and HDR10+ look gorgeous. Colors pop, and contrast is great. It also gets bright -- plenty bright for a living room during the daytime. There are a good amount of picture settings to play with, brightness/contrast/local dimming/AI stuff, etc so it may take you a bit to get everything dialed in, but once you do, *chef's kiss* Is it the best TV out there? Of course not. Is it the best TV for the price point? Absolutely yes. Pictures are undoctored, cell phone camera tries, but doesn't do it justice. column5: LG - 48" Class C5 Series OLED evo AI 4K UHD Smart webOS TV (2025)
column8: review1 - The LG C5 is truly amazing. Aside from the obvious picture detail, the brightness in this TV is great. Especially if you are in a darker room as I am. I have lights on, but they are not bright. If you are in a super bright room, then OLED may not be way to go or QD-OLED might a better option for you as this is a W-OLED. The C5 offers 1 major thing I personally love and that is being able to adjust a lot of the settings. Some OLEDs don't allow it and some allow very few customizations. Here I am able to adjust both Brightness AND Peak Brightness along with the Aspect Ratio, Color Depth, tint, white balance, clarity, resolution and more. If you are coming from Roku or Google TV then Web OS will be different but not bad at all. If you stay on the menu long, then eventually a moveable screen saver appears. Those who use Apple 4k TV will know exactly what it is. For Web OS you are able to remove the ADs that pop up so keep that in mind if you are like me and do not like ADs at all. LG gave you the option to remove them. Sound Quality is good, but I can't speak much to it since I use headphones most of the time. From what I can hear, I would definitely look into a soundbar if you are big into movies or anime. Burn in will always be there BUT it is very rare now days. Make sure you turn on the OLED care features. This automatically adjust the pixels. The only people that should worry about burn in now days are those that use it on 1 channel for 8-12 hours a day. Those people are usually the ones that watch FOX News or CNN but this happens around 2000-3000 hours of everyday usage which is about 8-12 months in. The TV also has a feature that if you want to leave a channel on all day but mainly for background noise or want to listen to music on your TV then you can turn off the screen while the TV is still on. This is a GREAT feature I personally use. But just use your TV. Don't get too caught up online with burn in because it will make you question everything and the point of you getting a new TV is for you to enjoy it. ||| review2 - This tv is incredible! column8: review1 - We recently upgraded to the TCL 98" QM9K, and it has completely transformed our home theater. At this size, picture quality matters, and the QM9K delivers in a big way. The brightness is phenomenal, HDR highlights really pop, and the Mini-LED local dimming does an impressive job with contrast and black levels, especially for a non-OLED display. Colors are vibrant without being over-saturated, motion handling is excellent, and sports, movies, and streaming content all look fantastic. For a 98-inch screen, the image remains sharp and immersive even at closer viewing distances. Google TV runs smoothly and is easy to navigate, and setup was straightforward. We paired it with a Sonos soundbar via eARC with no issues. For a screen this large, the panel uniformity and build quality are excellent. The biggest takeaway is value. At this price point, it’s hard to imagine anything else that competes with the QM9K’s combination of size, brightness, and overall performance. Comparable models from other brands are significantly more expensive. Huge credit to Best Buy and Geek Squad as well — delivery and installation were included, professional, and stress-free, which is no small thing when you’re dealing with a 98-inch TV. If you’re considering a true big-screen upgrade and want flagship-level impact without paying flagship prices, the TCL QM9K is an easy recommendation. ||| review2 - Impressive blacks with a nice finish. I am disappointed in Best Buy; not only am I a BB Total member (which offers free TV Mounting) but Mounting costs (up to $339) was included as a Black Friday bonus. I prepped everything as required before the Geak Squad arrived (I even had a wall outlet installed) but they refused to mount it, they said my Vesa-600 mount wouldn't work for this Vesa-600 TV. *Not only did the mount work (i ended up Mounting it myself) but TCL confirmed by email that it would work. I have to say it’s a large TV when you first see it but after watching for a little while it seems a perfect fit. Very bright and clear picture ||| review6 - The TCL 98QM9K is a cinematic marvel. It's also spectacular for gaming. I've owned my fair share of QD-Mini LED's and the 98QM9K is easily in another league. Before diving into this review, I think it's important to note that my 98QM9K is running the latest firmware (V8-0012T03-LF1V039.001875) which seems to have just recently been released on February 14, 2026. My experience so far has been near flawless with some very minor quirks that TCL can hopefully address in future firmware updates. I would realistically give the 98QM9k a 4.5/5 rating if I was able to but I didn't feel that deducting an entire point was representative of how impressive it performs in it's core areas. It's not perfect, but it's darn close. Also, because my living room has a ton of windows, this QM9K performs better in one key area that no other current Mini-LED or OLED panel on the market is able to compete with (other than TCL's X11L of course); it's brightness! Due to it's whopping 6,500 nits of peak brightness, I could hardly ask for a better TV that's suited for my living room. I was pleasantly surprised with how the TV gets shipped from TCL. The bottom of the TV is strapped onto a form-fitting palette that helps provide stability to the TV while it's in the upright position. This was very convenient for me as I needed to store the TV in the garage until help arrived to lift this beast into my home. While this 98" can be unboxed with two people, I highly recommend having three people to help. It's truly massive and heavy. A thoughtful inclusion by TCL was designing the bottom styrofoam in such a way that it allows you to use it as a temporary resting stand while putting on the TV feet. The TV feet allows you to set them up in two different height variations. I LOVE that TCL included this feature as it allowed me to get just enough clearance in between the bottom lip of the TV and my TV stand for my Dolby Atmos soundbar. The build quality on the QM9K is top notch. I love the sleek design with it's ultra thin metal bezels. The back of the panel also features premium hard cover speaker grills for the Bang & Olufsen drivers. The placement and design of the IR sensor is also brilliant. Even though the top of my soundbar seems to practically cover the sensor, navigating the UI with the remote control has been flawless; even in situations where my remote is not pointing directly at the sensor. This was an annoying issue with my previous Mini-LED TV whereby I had to buy an IR blaster extender because my soundbar partially covered the sensor. Not an issue with the QM9K! While the included remote maintains a sleek metallic appearance, I do wish that it was a bit higher quality. The top part of the remote has a very thin sheet of aluminum that feels a bit "plasticky". The rest of the remote is just black plastic. I would have loved to have seen at least 50% of the remote being constructed of brushed aluminum. I also would have liked to have seen a dedicated "Play/Pause" button on the remote. Rubber buttons over plastic buttons would have also been a nice touch. However, I do really love that the touch-sensitive buttons are all backlit. I've also really enjoyed the seamless operation of the IR blaster and sensor; despite how many obstructions there seems to be from my remote to my TV. In terms of image quality, it's hard to contain your excitement once you start watching your favorite movies and TV shows on the 98QM9K. I've watched Dolby Vision, HDR10+, and HDR10 content on streaming apps and on 4K blu-rays. It blows me away every time. First of all, for being a Mini-LED TV, backlight bloom was hardly noticeable for me on any of the content I've watched so far. As with any Mini-LED panel, some degree of backlight bloom will always exist but it is extremely minimal with the QM9K. When watching the aforementioned ultra HD formats, I was very impressed with the QM9K's ability to handle HDR tone mapping, it's white uniformity, shadow level details, and it's ability to produce organic looking skin tones. The QM9K also has EXCEPTIONAL contrast. With that said, depending on the type of content I was watching, I did find myself having to re-calibrate some of the factory image settings to my liking. Out of the box, I noticed that TCL likes to max out the color temperature to "Warm" in a lot of its presets. While the warm color temperature does look quite good on most content, I did find that I preferred a more balanced temperature for certain content. Once image settings were adjusted, the image quality was phenomenal. For example, turning on "Dynamic Tone Mapping" and setting it to "Balance" really enhanced 4K animated movies such as Pixar's "Ratatouille". The brightness was auto-adjusted to really bring out the details in the characters. With it off, while the picture quality still looked great, some of the scenes didn't appear as lush or as detailed as they did with it on. I did notice that I had to be a bit cautious with settings like "Dynamic Acceleration". This setting is supposed to increase screen refresh rate. When I enabled it while watching my 4K Blu-ray of Ratatouille, I initially liked it because it did seem to make the motion appear a bit more fluid. However, I noticed that in certain scenes it would introduce some strange artifacts. In the scene where Remy stumbles into Gusteau's kitchen for the first time, and accidentally hitches a ride onto the food cart, there was some weird green artifacts that were introduced on the edges of the wheels as well as on the outlines of certain characters in the scene. When I turned it off and replayed the scene, these artifacts would no longer appear. So depending on the content, your mileage may vary in terms of how it may impact the image. "Vivid" was my favorite preset for 4K HDR10 animated content. Vivid adds a little more color saturation and turns on the following: dynamic tone mapping to priority brightness, dynamic contrast to high, micro contrast, and dynamic color. It also boosts the sharpness! This looked fantastic for animated movies but it wasn't a preset I found myself using a lot for live-action movies. I did still have to turn down the "Motion Clarity" to "Medium" as "High" still introduced a bit of motion artifacting. For ultra HD live action content, I let the QM9K auto-select the preset and then fine-tuned some settings to my preference. I love that once you make your adjustments for the selected preset, the TV allows you to save those settings for the input it's currently on, and gives you the option to apply it to all other inputs as well. I found that for Dolby Vision content, "Dolby Vision IQ" and "Dolby Vision Bright" produced a gorgeous image. I mainly adjusted the color temperature, color, and dark detail to my preference. I deliberately chose to watch Alien Romulus, 1917, and Andor for their dark scenes. I used Dune 2 to test both ends of the dynamic range since it features a lot of high contrast bright desert scenes, as well as some very low-light sequences. Skin tones looked very natural, colors were rich and vibrant, and black levels were very inky. Black shadow details were also very good for a Mini-LED. I don't think they are quite flagship OLED quality yet, but it's getting very close. I have yet to experience any type of black crush or banding. Watching sports also looks beautiful on this panel. I do feel that the "Sports" preset over saturates the color though. I had to turn down the "Color" to "50" and adjust the color temperature. I also had to turn off "Dynamic Color" as it would overshoot some of the colors and lose quite a bit of color accuracy. I was just as impressed with the gaming performance of this TV as I was with it's image quality. I connected my PS5, Nintendo Switch 2, and played several titles like Elden Ring, FF7 Rebirth, Mario vs Donkey Kong, Street Fighter 6, and several others. The TV auto-detects when a gaming console is connected to an input and automatically applies all the optimized gaming settings. It automatically selects "game" for the picture mode and also applies the "game master" mode. I love that TCL took the guess work out of having to manually fiddle with additional settings to optimize gaming visual fidelity. "Game Master" automatically enabled ALLM (Auto Low Latency mode) and 144Hz VRR. It apparently also disables unnecessary image processing. The one thing that took me a while to figure out was how to bring up the game bar (please add a dedicated button on the remote, TCL!). You have to hold down the button with 3 horizontal lines on it, for about 3 seconds, until the game bar comes up. This allows you to use additional features like displaying the FPS counter, adjusting shadow enhancement, choosing different game picture modes, etc. All my games ran buttery smooth and I didn't experience any noticeable input lag. No noticeable issues with ghosting, or pixel trailing, either. The only time I did encounter an issue with VRR was in Hogwarts Legacy. For whatever reason, when enabled, I would experience a bit of input lag. Once I turned VRR off, I would experience a notable improvement with how quickly my button actions would be displayed on-screen. It's possible that I may need to play with some of the in-game performance settings for this particular game but I didn't experience this with any other titles that I tried with VRR enabled. All in all, the visuals looked great and features like AMD Freesync's VRR kept games running smoothly. I think the 98QM9K delivers a stellar cinematic experience that is very close to OLED. In certain scenes, it's indistinguishable unless you have them side by side. And with the only available OLED options in this screen size costing as much as a car, the 98QM9K is an obvious choice for many! ||| review7 - I’ve had several tcl TVs ranging from the 65 inch QM8 mini led (2023 model), TCL 55 inch nxtframe (edge lit) and now this new 2025 model QM9k. So I know the quality from low-ish to highest end tcl QM9k 98 inch beautiful beast of a tv both in size and quality. This 4k mini led tv is nearly perfect with its large size up to 6k local dimming zone to keep black levels near that of oled and help the overall picture quality look more detailed with helping the contrast between dark and light scenes. Very very little bloom if any to my eyes thanks to TCL “halo control” seems to do its job. Colors are vivid as you would expect from a tier this high both in hdr+ and Dolby vision looking its best while watching anything 4k. 1080p looks good as well(I have the basic nexflix and hbo max) though have to say, the up scaling is good but not the best I have seen compared to other TVs I’ve had but not a deal breaker in my opinion. Still very good maybe I’m picky lol. Brightness is probably its main claim to fame as I believe it’s the highest nit tv out as of now. While I agree it’s very bright, it is not blinding at all even at full brightness and the peak brightness setting at boost. Maybe it’s because it’s such a large tv or the processor management is that good I’m not sure but its bright and makes the content you are watching pop. Refresh rate is 144hz max.great for gaming if you want to hook a PC but latency if never as good as an oled monitor but it’s a nice option if you want to use it. I mainly watch tv and play ps5. All the gaming features you need with plenty of customization with game bar being a plus and very useful. It’s a Google tv with Gemini and of course it’s the best platform to use on any tv works great and smooth no issues. Speakers are very good for being tuned by audio partner bang & olufsen. Not a replacement for a dedicated surround or even a decent sound bar but does sound good enough to impress any of your guests for sure. Design is very stylish and relatively slim. Remote has every button you need and is backlit which I love. Overall a beautiful tv from picture quality to design. But one thing I don’t love is the fact that this tv I know is huge and you should have wide separation between the legs you are forced to buy a new and probably expensive wide tv stand to accommodate this big and heavy tv. They should have 2 options for legs because I had to buy and after market tv mounted legs that went closer in and it is steady. Minor gripe but at this price point that should be a definite option for the consumer imo. Again. It the end of the world but something to note. Check specs on Bestbuy website. A definite recommendation from me a huge techy but as long as your budget allows. I love it! ||| review8 - The TCL – 98” Class QM9K Series 4K TV offers a premium experience by combining top tier hardware and features including ultra-bright QD-Mini LED Technology, Dolby Vision IQ/Dolby Atmos, 144 Hz Native Refresh Rate, and Auto Game Mode with Game Accelerator 288 making it a top contender for best-in-class home theater and gaming TV. • Unboxing – This thing is massive and takes two people to safely move and unbox. It weighs approximately 123.5 lbs according to the product information sheet. It arrived via scheduled freight delivery on a pallet and was well packaged to prevent damage. It's also spectacular for gaming. I've owned my fair share of QD-Mini LED's and the 98QM9K is easily in another league. Before diving into this review, I think it's important to note that my 98QM9K is running the latest firmware (V8-0012T03-LF1V039.001875) which seems to have just recently been released on February 14, 2026. My experience so far has been near flawless with some very minor quirks that TCL can hopefully address in future firmware updates. I would realistically give the 98QM9k a 4.5/5 rating if I was able to but I didn't feel that deducting an entire point was representative of how impressive it performs in it's core areas. It's not perfect, but it's darn close. Also, because my living room has a ton of windows, this QM9K performs better in one key area that no other current Mini-LED or OLED panel on the market is able to compete with (other than TCL's X11L of course); it's brightness! Due to it's whopping 6,500 nits of peak brightness, I could hardly ask for a better TV that's suited for my living room. I was pleasantly surprised with how the TV gets shipped from TCL. The bottom of the TV is strapped onto a form-fitting palette that helps provide stability to the TV while it's in the upright position. This was very convenient for me as I needed to store the TV in the garage until help arrived to lift this beast into my home. While this 98" can be unboxed with two people, I highly recommend having three people to help. It's truly massive and heavy. A thoughtful inclusion by TCL was designing the bottom styrofoam in such a way that it allows you to use it as a temporary resting stand while putting on the TV feet. The TV feet allows you to set them up in two different height variations. I LOVE that TCL included this feature as it allowed me to get just enough clearance in between the bottom lip of the TV and my TV stand for my Dolby Atmos soundbar. The build quality on the QM9K is top notch. I love the sleek design with it's ultra thin metal bezels. The back of the panel also features premium hard cover speaker grills for the Bang & Olufsen drivers. The placement and design of the IR sensor is also brilliant. Even though the top of my soundbar seems to practically cover the sensor, navigating the UI with the remote control has been flawless; even in situations where my remote is not pointing directly at the sensor. This was an annoying issue with my previous Mini-LED TV whereby I had to buy an IR blaster extender because my soundbar partially covered the sensor. Not an issue with the QM9K! While the included remote maintains a sleek metallic appearance, I do wish that it was a bit higher quality. The top part of the remote has a very thin sheet of aluminum that feels a bit "plasticky". The rest of the remote is just black plastic. I would have loved to have seen at least 50% of the remote being constructed of brushed aluminum. I also would have liked to have seen a dedicated "Play/Pause" button on the remote. Rubber buttons over plastic buttons would have also been a nice touch. However, I do really love that the touch-sensitive buttons are all backlit. I've also really enjoyed the seamless operation of the IR blaster and sensor; despite how many obstructions there seems to be from my remote to my TV. In terms of image quality, it's hard to contain your excitement once you start watching your favorite movies and TV shows on the 98QM9K. I've watched Dolby Vision, HDR10+, and HDR10 content on streaming apps and on 4K blu-rays. It blows me away every time. First of all, for being a Mini-LED TV, backlight bloom was hardly noticeable for me on any of the content I've watched so far. As with any Mini-LED panel, some degree of backlight bloom will always exist but it is extremely minimal with the QM9K. When watching the aforementioned ultra HD formats, I was very impressed with the QM9K's ability to handle HDR tone mapping, it's white uniformity, shadow level details, and it's ability to produce organic looking skin tones. The QM9K also has EXCEPTIONAL contrast. With that said, depending on the type of content I was watching, I did find myself having to re-calibrate some of the factory image settings to my liking. Out of the box, I noticed that TCL likes to max out the color temperature to "Warm" in a lot of its presets. While the warm color temperature does look quite good on most content, I did find that I preferred a more balanced temperature for certain content. Once image settings were adjusted, the image quality was phenomenal. For example, turning on "Dynamic Tone Mapping" and setting it to "Balance" really enhanced 4K animated movies such as Pixar's "Ratatouille". The brightness was auto-adjusted to really bring out the details in the characters. With it off, while the picture quality still looked great, some of the scenes didn't appear as lush or as detailed as they did with it on. I did notice that I had to be a bit cautious with settings like "Dynamic Acceleration". This setting is supposed to increase screen refresh rate. When I enabled it while watching my 4K Blu-ray of Ratatouille, I initially liked it because it did seem to make the motion appear a bit more fluid. However, I noticed that in certain scenes it would introduce some strange artifacts. In the scene where Remy stumbles into Gusteau's kitchen for the first time, and accidentally hitches a ride onto the food cart, there was some weird green artifacts that were introduced on the edges of the wheels as well as on the outlines of certain characters in the scene. When I turned it off and replayed the scene, these artifacts would no longer appear. So depending on the content, your mileage may vary in terms of how it may impact the image. "Vivid" was my favorite preset for 4K HDR10 animated content. Vivid adds a little more color saturation and turns on the following: dynamic tone mapping to priority brightness, dynamic contrast to high, micro contrast, and dynamic color. It also boosts the sharpness! This looked fantastic for animated movies but it wasn't a preset I found myself using a lot for live-action movies. I did still have to turn down the "Motion Clarity" to "Medium" as "High" still introduced a bit of motion artifacting. For ultra HD live action content, I let the QM9K auto-select the preset and then fine-tuned some settings to my preference. I love that once you make your adjustments for the selected preset, the TV allows you to save those settings for the input it's currently on, and gives you the option to apply it to all other inputs as well. I found that for Dolby Vision content, "Dolby Vision IQ" and "Dolby Vision Bright" produced a gorgeous image. I mainly adjusted the color temperature, color, and dark detail to my preference. I deliberately chose to watch Alien Romulus, 1917, and Andor for their dark scenes. I used Dune 2 to test both ends of the dynamic range since it features a lot of high contrast bright desert scenes, as well as some very low-light sequences. Skin tones looked very natural, colors were rich and vibrant, and black levels were very inky. Black shadow details were also very good for a Mini-LED. I don't think they are quite flagship OLED quality yet, but it's getting very close. I have yet to experience any type of black crush or banding. Watching sports also looks beautiful on this panel. I do feel that the "Sports" preset over saturates the color though. I had to turn down the "Color" to "50" and adjust the color temperature. I also had to turn off "Dynamic Color" as it would overshoot some of the colors and lose quite a bit of color accuracy. I was just as impressed with the gaming performance of this TV as I was with it's image quality. I connected my PS5, Nintendo Switch 2, and played several titles like Elden Ring, FF7 Rebirth, Mario vs Donkey Kong, Street Fighter 6, and several others. The TV auto-detects when a gaming console is connected to an input and automatically applies all the optimized gaming settings. It automatically selects "game" for the picture mode and also applies the "game master" mode. I love that TCL took the guess work out of having to manually fiddle with additional settings to optimize gaming visual fidelity. "Game Master" automatically enabled ALLM (Auto Low Latency mode) and 144Hz VRR. It apparently also disables unnecessary image processing. The one thing that took me a while to figure out was how to bring up the game bar (please add a dedicated button on the remote, TCL!). You have to hold down the button with 3 horizontal lines on it, for about 3 seconds, until the game bar comes up. This allows you to use additional features like displaying the FPS counter, adjusting shadow enhancement, choosing different game picture modes, etc. All my games ran buttery smooth and I didn't experience any noticeable input lag. No noticeable issues with ghosting, or pixel trailing, either. The only time I did encounter an issue with VRR was in Hogwarts Legacy. For whatever reason, when enabled, I would experience a bit of input lag. Once I turned VRR off, I would experience a notable improvement with how quickly my button actions would be displayed on-screen. It's possible that I may need to play with some of the in-game performance settings for this particular game but I didn't experience this with any other titles that I tried with VRR enabled. All in all, the visuals looked great and features like AMD Freesync's VRR kept games running smoothly. I think the 98QM9K delivers a stellar cinematic experience that is very close to OLED. In certain scenes, it's indistinguishable unless you have them side by side. And with the only available OLED options in this screen size costing as much as a car, the 98QM9K is an obvious choice for many! ||| review7 - I’ve had several tcl TVs ranging from the 65 inch QM8 mini led (2023 model), TCL 55 inch nxtframe (edge lit) and now this new 2025 model QM9k. Still very good maybe I’m picky lol. Brightness is probably its main claim to fame as I believe it’s the highest nit tv out as of now. While I agree it’s very bright, it is not blinding at all even at full brightness and the peak brightness setting at boost. Maybe it’s because it’s such a large tv or the processor management is that good I’m not sure but its bright and makes the content you are watching pop. A definite recommendation from me a huge techy but as long as your budget allows. I love it! ||| review8 - The TCL – 98” Class QM9K Series 4K TV offers a premium experience by combining top tier hardware and features including ultra-bright QD-Mini LED Technology, Dolby Vision IQ/Dolby Atmos, 144 Hz Native Refresh Rate, and Auto Game Mode with Game Accelerator 288 making it a top contender for best-in-class home theater and gaming TV. • Unboxing – This thing is massive and takes two people to safely move and unbox. You will not regret it! ||| review9 - **** Summary **** The TCL QM9K is my first foray into the really-big TV category, as well as the Quantum Dot mini LED technology, and I was blown away by how nice it is. The QM9K’s 98” display is big and very expansive, and the picture quality and brightness are superb. It’s been excellent for everything – movies and TV shows, watching 4K YouTube videos, and playing games on it. Even the sound system was impressive with its way better than expected soundstage and bass output. You know the saying that “Once you go big, you can’t go back” or “Go big or go home”? That’s so true of the 98” QM9K because the size DOES affect your immersion experience when viewing content, making the viewer feel like you’re inside a small movie theater. It’s a Win~! ______ *Pros: -Big, thin-bezel 98” screen with excellent brightness, color spectrum, and even lighting. -Clear voice, very decent bass, and excellent loudness. -Plenty of ports on the back. -Gaming performance is very good at 4K@120Hz. -The TV interface and menu system are snappy and easy to navigate. -Google TV with Gemini AI built-in is useful. -Very responsive remote control with great button feel and intuitive placement. -Direct buttons for Prime Video, Netflix, YouTube, and Gemini. -You can connect an external hard drive via the USB port and watch your multimedia content without lag. -Excellent value. ______ *Neutral: -144Hz at 4K results in jitter and doesn’t work correctly. ______ *Cons: -None **** The Setup **** When I laid my eyes on the humongous and heavy box, I felt daunted about how I was going to unpack the TV and get it set up. Fortunately, thanks to the cleverly designed external cardboard box and strategically placed foam blocks, the unpacking process was a non-issue, granted you have at least two people to help you during the process (to prevent tip-over and remove packaging pieces). With the cardboard box removed and the TV balanced on the center foam block and someone holding the TV steady, it was easy enough to attach the two TV leg stands and tighten the bolts. Although assembly was simple and easy, the challenging part was getting it lifted and placed on top of our TV stand which is about 4” high. My wife wasn’t strong enough to lift the ~120lb TV, so I had to recruit my neighbor to do so. The TV stands are stable for the most part, but the panel will wobble if you try to shake it. So I placed some 6lb dumbbells on top of the rear portion of the TV leg stands for stability, and it’s now very stable and steady. **** Performance, Features and Viewing Experience **** With its 98” screen real estate, 3.2mm thin bezel, 6042 local dimming zones, 6500 nits peak brightness, support for an array of HDR formats (Dolby Vision, HDR 10, HDR 10+, HLG), and the Bang & Olufsen 2.1 sound system, the QM9K really cranks up the immersion factor when watching anything on it. Everything feels so fresh and new, even if it’s a movie or a YouTube clip you’ve seen before on a different (and smaller) screen, simply due to the sheer expansiveness of the 98” screen, the high brightness, and high color fidelity and accuracy. I think the phrase “Everything old is new again” sums up my experience with the QM9K very well, and I love it for that because it truly and deeply increased the satisfaction and pleasure I derive when watching movies and TV shows I’ve been especially waiting for (like Fallout Season 2). As I mentioned before, the audio is very decent for a TV, but it’s not super fantastic enough to eschew a soundbar system. So not too long after the setup of the TV, I connected my 7.1.4-channel Samsung soundbar system to the eARC port, which increased the immersion factor another notch. With a 98” big screen and the 7.1.4 speakers firing off from multiple directions, I really felt like I was inside a small and private movie theater of my very own. Being in my forties, I don’t feel giddy very often anymore, but the QM9K revived such emotions. It’s often not mentioned in many reviews, but I applaud TCL for the performant and snappy chipset they installed in the QM9K that makes menu and input switching and menu navigation such a quick and frustration-free experience. My old 55” TV had an anemic processor so it couldn’t quickly open folders and launch video files from a hard drive that I connected to it (via the USB port). The QM9K with its AIPQ Pro Processor, on the other hand, is so powerful, navigating through multiple folders and video files on my external hard drive was super snappy and lag-free, which made me VERY happy. Seriously, big TVs are so nice. If you don’t have the coin for it right now, then I suggest saving up and getting a nice TV like the 98” TCL QM9K, because if you enjoy your movies, YouTube, and TV shows, then you’ll experience a real and profound “upgrade” in your entertainment life experience by going bigger and brighter. Oh, and don’t forget to pair it up with a good sound system. **** Gaming Performance **** I was slightly disappointed with the QM9K because I could not stably enable the 144Hz refresh option on my Nvidia GeForce 5800 equipped gaming laptop. The moment I select the 144Hz dropdown option, the screen began to jitter and artifact like crazy. Once I dropped it back down to 120Hz, everything was good again. I downloaded and installed the latest firmware, but 144Hz was still a no-go on my Windows 11 gaming laptop. To be honest, however, it’s not a big deal, because my laptop isn’t powerful enough to run the latest games at 4K and at 144Hz refresh rate. Besides the small hiccup with the 144Hz refresh rate issue, everything else was just fine and peachy, and gaming never felt better, with such rich colors, high clarity, and brightness. **** Is it worth the coin? **** Absolutely. With the QM9K often going on sale and dipping much below its $5999.99 MSRP price, it’s a fantastic value and an excellent deal. If you don’t believe me, then search for head-to-head comparisons against TVs that cost 2-3 times more from reputable publications, and you’ll see that the QM9K offers cutting-edge and up-to-date technology, high performance, and a great value against the majority of other TVs with similar specs. To be honest, before taking a chance on the TCL QM9K, I usually only stuck with the “safe” big brand name labels because I was so afraid of making a mistake. But TCL has shown me that they are just as cutting-edge and adept at making fantastic-looking and sounding TVs that can not only hang with the big boys but come out on top as well. I love my 98” TCL QM9K TV, and I think you’ll too. 5 Stars Win. ||| review10 - I’m upgrading from an 85”, which sadly has started to appear small over the past year lol. Once powered on, both my friends phone and my phone were signaled by the TV asking us to connect our account. Aside from the size, one of my first impressions was how fast and responsive the TV worked while navigating it! A lot of TV’s that have built in systems for streaming will have some lag or sluggishness, this one was a breath of fresh air and works quickly! Next is the picture quality. I like to run tests and really dig in visually to try to look for blooming, halos, over saturation, or bad pixels that may exist. My out of the box experience was good, we first watched Tron for its high contrast of colors. I was actually pretty impressed with it. I’m a huge OLED fan, but don’t like how they don’t get very bright. Non-OLED tv’s struggle getting dark blacks, but wow these were pretty close to OLED in my opinion. I currently have it in Movie mode, and I like to reference rtings.com calibration settings for TVs, and play around with them. I also like to play demo videos to really get the colors to pop out since your average show doesn’t really push the colors to the limit. Check out Jennifer Gala on youtube, lots of great videos to see your TVs potential and great for making your TV look like it does at Best Buy when playing those demos. I love how it has 4 HDMI ports, 2 for 144hz (gaming) and 2 for 60hz (movies & shows), all of which are easily accessible from the right side of the TV and clearly labeled along with the other ports. As a computer nerd, I do appreciate having an ethernet port as well. I did have some issues with Gemini AI assistant not working, even though it was enabled and I do pay for the premium AI service already, but that is more from Google TV than the TCL tv side. Overall, its been a great tv and nice upgrade from what I’ve had. I’ve watched movies, shows, football games, and several TV demos on it, all leaving me excited to watch more. I do like compatibility of HDR options that come with it, especially since my last TV did not have Dolby Vision. I hosted a Superbowl party and everyone was shocked by the size of the TV and really enjoyed the quality of it. Despite not being an OLED panel, the Mini LEDs do a great job with color contrast and provide near-perfect black levels. The 144 Hz refresh rate ensures gameplay remains smooth. I can’t comment specifically on the Bang and Olufsen speakers because we have our TV connected through the HDMI eARC port to a surround sound system. I’m sure they’re great. One thing I can say is that a frequent issue we had with our previous TV is the connection between said TV and our surround sound system (also through HDMI eARC) would randomly, and frequently disconnect and require a reboot. A simple thing, but intensely annoying. We have had no such issue with this TCL TV. Processing power overall seems solid as there has been no lag with powering on, scrolling through and selecting apps, or using remote voice commands. We love this TV and hope it last a really long time! There are a few things that we encountered during setup that I think folks should be aware of if you are looking to buy this TV. As the title of my review alludes to, a 98” TV is extremely large. We had it delivered to our home and it required a scheduled delivery date and time via freight. Its packaging is just like any new TV, but because of its size, there is just naturally more styrofoam and cardboard. Be prepared to cut up lots of large cardboard panels if you don’t have access to a dumpster size recycling bin. If you choose to mount the TV, be mindful of the VESA pattern/compatibility. I purchased a mount prior to receiving the TV that said it would accommodate TVs up to 98”, but I found out way after the fact that it did not accommodate the 600mm x 500mm VESA pattern that this TV has. I had to go out a buy another mount, which wasted time and ended up being quite a bit more expensive. Alas. The final thing I want to mention is if you are planning to mount the TV on your own, be ready. The TV without the stand only weighs in at 121.3 pounds, but because it’s distributed over such a large surface area, it’s awkward and VERY difficult to lift. With just two people, we used multiple chairs to systematically lift one side at a time and eventually got it, but really put our marriage to the test in the process. I upgraded from a 65” standard LED TV, and honestly, I wasn’t expecting to be this impressed—especially considering how much more affordable this set was compared to some of the big-name brands. Picture Quality: The picture on this TV is insanely good for the price. The mini-LED backlighting makes a noticeable difference, especially in darker scenes. column5: TCL - 98" X11L Series 4K UHD HDR SQD-Mini LED Smart TV with Google TV (2026)
column8: review1 - I fell in love with this TV the first time I saw it at CES, and now that I have it at home, it has completely exceeded my expectations. The brightness is on another level. With up to 10,000 nits and 20,000 dimming zones in a massive 98” screen, the picture is absolutely stunning. Highlights pop, blacks stay deep, and the color volume is incredible. It’s one of those TVs you truly have to see in person to appreciate. Pictures and videos don’t do it justice. Yes, it’s expensive. But when you compare it to OLED options in this size, it’s nearly half the price and significantly brighter. In a bright room especially, this TV really shines. The size combined with this level of brightness and contrast makes it feel like a true home theater experience. If you’re looking for a flagship 98” TV and want jaw-dropping performance, this is it. ||| review2 - This TCL 98 X11L is a beautiful and massive TV. It’s not only huge but also very heavy, despite being thin at approximately an inch thick. The TV is very well made with a premium look and feel. The frame has a bronze tone, and the screen appears almost bezel-less. The back is practically flat with a checker-style design. It comes with a Bang & Olufsen speaker system for premium sound. On the back, it houses four HDMI 2.1 ports capable of 4K at up to 144Hz, with one supporting eARC. It also includes one USB 3.0 port, two USB 2.0 ports, an optical output (SPDIF), and an Ethernet jack. The TV is powered by Google TV, which I really like because of its simplicity and compatibility. When it comes to technology, it’s packed. The main highlight is the SQD Mini-LED panel, which makes this TV one of the brightest available, reaching up to 10,000 nits. It also supports Dolby Vision, Dolby Atmos FlexConnect (DAFC), DTS:X, Chromecast, Apple AirPlay 2, Alexa, Google Assistant, Apple HomeKit, Wi-Fi 6, and Bluetooth 5.4. Before taking the TV out of the box, make sure you have a second person and plenty of space. It will definitely take at least two people to set it up, as it weighs almost 150 pounds. Be careful not to cut the tape on the top of the box, just cut the plastic straps. The box opens sideways once you remove the clips holding it together. After that, you simply pull the box from one side to remove it. If you plan to use the TV stand, leave the TV sitting in the bottom styrofoam and remove one side of the bottom foam at a time to install the stand. There is a center foam support that helps keep the TV stable, while the second person holds it to prevent it from rocking. This also makes lifting easier because the TV will already be a few inches off the ground. If you plan to wall mount, leaving the bottom styrofoam in place actually makes the process easier. Once the hard part is done, setup is very simple, especially if you already have an Android device or a Gmail account. All you need to do is scan a QR code, or login with Gmail and follow the prompts. Between the setup process and system updates, it took a little over 20 minutes to complete. The Google TV interface is simple to navigate, fluid, and includes most major streaming apps. Watching Blu-Ray and streaming content on this TV I was impressed. I didn't adjust any video settings aside from using the Film Maker Mode. The image quality is stunning and extremely bright. Colors are vivid and vibrant, with deep blacks that get very close to OLED performance, coming from a person that owns two OLEDs TV. Now I understand why there’s so much hype about SQD Mini-LED technology. I didn’t notice any image banding except briefly during the startup screen when the TCL logo appeared bright white against a black background. While the picture is incredibly sharp on such a massive screen, the panel itself is glossy, which makes it susceptible to light reflections. In my living room, there are about four windows and a door, and I could see some reflections from the window shades. However, when focusing on the content on the screen, the reflections become much less noticeable. They were more visible when viewing from an angle. That said, viewing angles are excellent. Even from the side, the colors remain vibrant and consistent, almost as good as viewing directly from the front. This TV is also excellent for gaming. It supports 4K at 144Hz, VRR, AMD FreeSync Premium Pro, HDR, and Dolby Vision for gaming. The panel is natively 120Hz, but to activate 144Hz, you need to access the gaming settings by holding down the settings button (hamburger button) on the remote. I connected my Xbox, gaming laptop and PS5 and they performed incredibly smoothly. One thing I noticed is that games supporting Dolby Vision tend to appear a bit dark by default. I had to manually switch to Bright mode, which in my opinion looked much better. Note that due to the large size of this TV, when playing video games, especially fast-paced shooters, it’s best to sit farther away to minimize head movement. I played my favorite shooter from about 10 feet away and didn’t have to move my head, I only needed to shift my eye focus a few times. When it comes to sound, it’s good but not great, despite having an integrated soundbar with base radiators on the back. While it gets loud and remains clear, it lacks bass for my taste. I tried various sound settings, but they didn’t make much difference. The integrated system is decent for a TV of this size, but I would still recommend pairing it with a dedicated soundbar or TCL DAFC-compatible speakers. I would have loved to test Dolby Atmos FlexConnect, but I don’t own the TCL Z100 speakers. Although I own DAFC speakers, they weren’t compatible since they are from a different brand. It appears DAFC may still be somewhat proprietary within certain ecosystems. Paying attention to details really matters, and a simple feature they added to the remote is something I really appreciated. On the side of the remote, they included a brightness rocker button and an image selector button. It’s a very clever design, there’s no need to dig through the TV settings just to adjust the brightness or change the picture mode. I love it. Overall, this TV lives up to the hype with superb brightness, impressive image quality, and premium build quality. It’s packed with modern technology and, being such a large screen, it’s also excellent for gaming. While it’s definitely not cheap, you do get near-OLED image quality, higher brightness, a massive screen size, and no risk of burn-in. Inside the box you get the TV, remote control, two AA batteries, the stand, warranty card, and manuals. ||| review3 - INSTALL / SETUP This is not an easy setup—this thing is BIG and heavy. Wall mounting was honestly a pain due to the size and shape. If I had to do it again, I’d go professional install without hesitation. Cable management is a weak spot. There are small channels, but nothing substantial—when wall mounted, the TV can actually rest on the cables and sit slightly uneven. That’s something TCL should have solved on a premium set like this. BUILD / FEEL This feels like a premium TV—no question. Solid materials, very little flex, and the screen feels sturdy despite the size. The near bezel-less design gives it that floating picture look, and at 98 inches, it literally feels like a theater in your living room. I used a 3-stud wall mount for stability, and I’d recommend the same—don’t cut corners here. FEATURES / PERFORMANCE Google TV runs fast and smooth overall. Apps load quickly, live TV integration is clean, and it works well as a central media hub. There are some minor bugs—Netflix froze a couple of times—but nothing deal-breaking. Likely something that gets patched over time. The ambient screen saver with rotating artwork is actually a standout feature at this size—it turns the TV into a legit art display when idle. PICTURE QUALITY This is where the TV delivers. Black levels are deep—true black, not gray—and I didn’t notice any blooming around bright objects or subtitles, which is impressive for a Mini LED at this size. Colors are vibrant and controlled, and the brightness is borderline overwhelming—in a good way. HDR content pops hard. Honestly, depending on your room size, you may find yourself turning brightness down. BRIGHT ROOM PERFORMANCE The anti-glare coating does its job. There is some reflection, but it’s minimal considering the size of the screen. Brightness easily overpowers the room, and the Mini LED backlighting keeps colors consistent across the entire panel. Every inch of the screen feels evenly lit. UPSCALING (REALITY CHECK) Here’s the honest part—upscaling isn’t perfect. Non-4K content (especially YouTube) can look a bit soft and grainy. At 98 inches, flaws get exposed. If you mostly watch high-resolution content, it won’t bother you. But if you’re heavy into cable or lower-quality streams, you’ll notice it. MOTION / SPORTS Motion handling is excellent. With motion settings adjusted, I didn’t notice any blur, stutter, or that artificial “soap opera” effect. Fast action and sports stay smooth without looking fake. GAMING This thing is a monster for gaming. Tested on both PS5 and Xbox—144Hz feels incredibly smooth, input lag is minimal, and Game Mode is dialed in. Honestly, it should be called “Beast Mode.” The combination of refresh rate, deep blacks, and bright, saturated colors at 98 inches makes gaming feel next-level immersive. SOUND I run a 5.1 system, so I didn’t rely much on the built-in speakers. I listened to them briefly, they’re decent—but on a TV this size, “decent” isn’t enough. You’re going to want external audio to match the experience. DOWNSIDE One real drawback: design practicality doesn’t fully match the premium feel. • Cable management is lacking • Inputs are placed too far from the edges—hard to access once mounted • No included manual for a TV with this many settings • Remote is solid but not universal (missed opportunity) These aren’t deal-breakers—but they stand out at this price point. OVERALL A massive, theater-level TV with elite brightness, strong Mini LED performance, and top-tier gaming—just be ready to work around a few practical design misses. GREAT THEATER TV. ||| review4 - I have been team OLED for a while now. Once I realized the difference in colors and could clearly see the difference in a true OLED black and a LED greyish black, it was impossible for me to turn back. After the long process of unboxing the TCL X11L (which, makes sense, the packaging keeps the TV very secure) popping up the Netflix app to see it load up with the red with the all black background, I was blown away, and that was just the beginning. With so many things I loved about this TV, I'd like to start with the two small things I didn't. The TCL X11L is as high-end as it comes in regards to the tech that powers it, the features, etc. With that being said, I don't know why we're dealing with a remote that takes batteries. The remote is nice, the buttons are backlit...but we really shouldn't still be dealing with triple a batteries in 2026. Setup of the TV is super easy as it's a Android TV. QR code scan and in no time everything was setup. Now, the Google TV interface is nice...but it has tendency to make sponsored suggestions and attempt to recommend I watch content on it's free apps. Now, maybe, hopefully with abundance of paid subscriptions I have and use, the algorithm will pick up on what I truly like and watch...but man, being advertised to and pushed bloatware isn't a premium experience fitting of the rest of the device.
